use snapback4_lang::compile;

#[test]
fn project_builtins_are_reserved_for_parameters_locals_and_loop_bindings() {
    for (source, name) in [
        ("query q(now: time):\n  return now\n", "now"),
        ("mutation m():\n  commit = now\n  return commit\n", "commit"),
        ("mutation m():\n  for new in range(0, 1):\n    return new\n", "new"),
        ("query q(viewer: principal):\n  return viewer\n", "viewer"),
    ] {
        let bound = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
        let diagnostic = bound
            .diagnostics
            .iter()
            .find(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_RESERVED")
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{name}: {:?}", bound.diagnostics));
        assert!(diagnostic.message.contains(&format!("`{name}`")), "{diagnostic}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn repeated_identity_declarations_name_both_method_sets() {
    let same_file = compile(&[(
        "schema.q".into(),
        "use identity password\nuse identity guests\n".into(),
    )]);
    assert_eq!(same_file.diagnostics.len(), 1, "{:?}", same_file.diagnostics);
    let diagnostic = &same_file.diagnostics[0];
    assert_eq!(diagnostic.code, "E_QUARRY_SYNTAX");
    assert_eq!(diagnostic.site.line, 2);
    assert!(
        diagnostic.message.contains("password") && diagnostic.message.contains("guests"),
        "{diagnostic}"
    );

    let across_files = compile(&[
        ("schema.q".into(), "use identity guests\n".into()),
        ("accounts.q".into(), "use identity\n".into()),
    ]);
    assert_eq!(across_files.diagnostics.len(), 1, "{:?}", across_files.diagnostics);
    let diagnostic = &across_files.diagnostics[0];
    assert_eq!(diagnostic.site.file, "accounts.q");
    assert!(
        diagnostic.message.contains("guests")
            && diagnostic.message.contains("password and guests"),
        "{diagnostic}"
    );
}

fn diagnostic(source: &str, code: &str) -> snapback4_lang::Diagnostic {
    let bound = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
    bound
        .diagnostics
        .iter()
        .find(|diagnostic| diagnostic.code == code)
        .cloned()
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("missing {code}: {:#?}", bound.diagnostics))
}

fn replace_and_compile(source: &str, authored: &str, replacement: &str) {
    let repaired = source.replacen(authored, replacement, 1);
    assert_ne!(repaired, source, "fixture does not contain {authored:?}");
    let bound = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), repaired)]);
    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
}

//! E_QUARRY_RULE_OPERATOR: a table rule uses an expression rules do not
//! evaluate (an ordered comparison outside insert rules and named update
//! transitions, the clock, arithmetic or a helper call). The rewrite moves the
//! author's own comparison into the mutation as `require … else CODE`.

use crate::ast::Expr;
use crate::diag::{Diagnostic, Site};

/// What the rule language lacks for this term, if anything.
pub(super) fn unsupported_side(expr: &Expr) -> Option<&'static str> {
    match expr {
        Expr::Name { name, .. } if name == "now" => Some("the clock (`now`)"),
        Expr::Call { .. } => Some("a helper or function call"),
        Expr::Binary { op, .. } if matches!(op.as_str(), "+" | "-" | "*" | "/" | "%" | "??") => Some("arithmetic"),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// The effect a rule judges, as the author spelled it.
pub(super) fn effect_word(insert: bool, update: bool, read: bool) -> &'static str {
    if insert { "insert" } else if update { "update" } else if read { "read" } else { "delete" }
}

/// The refusal for one comparison `cmp` in a `table`'s `effect` rule.
pub(super) fn diagnostic(site: &Site, table: &str, effect: &str, transition: bool, cmp: &Expr, what: &str) -> Diagnostic {
    let text = strip_parens(&crate::print::expression(cmp));
    let field = first_field(&text).unwrap_or_else(|| "value".to_owned());
    let code = format!("INVALID_{}", screaming(&field));
    let message = format!("`{text}` in the {effect} rule of {table} uses {what}, which table rules do not evaluate: rules compare columns, viewer and literals with = and !=, and order (<, <=, >, >=) only an insert row's own required int, time, decimal or money columns and integer literals (minor units beside decimal or money), or old/next in a named update (old, next) rule");
    // The mutation names the stored row `row` and supplies new values as arguments.
    let stored = |image: Option<&str>, name: &str| match image { Some("next") => name.to_owned(), _ => format!("row.{name}") };
    let inserted = |_: Option<&str>, name: &str| name.to_owned();
    let rewrite = match effect {
        "insert" => {
            let mutation = map_fields(&text, &inserted);
            if what == "an ordered comparison" {
                format!("compare this row's own required int or time columns or an integer literal in the insert rule, or check it in the mutation that inserts the row: `require {mutation} else {code}`")
            } else {
                format!("check it in the mutation that inserts the row, using the values it inserts: `require {mutation} else {code}`")
            }
        }
        "update" if !transition && what == "an ordered comparison" => {
            let next = map_fields(&text, &|_, name| format!("next.{name}"));
            format!("name both images and bound the new one: `update (old, next) <- {next}`; or check it in the mutation: `row = {table}[id] ! else NOT_FOUND` then `require {} else {code}`", map_fields(&text, &stored))
        }
        "read" if what.contains("now") => match direct_focal_field(cmp) {
            Some(expires) => format!("a read rule is an audience, which cannot change with time: hide rows past this row's stored time with `expire at .{expires}`, or filter the query (`{table} where {} …`)", map_fields(&text, &|_, name| format!(".{name}"))),
            None => format!("a read rule is an audience, which cannot change with time: copy the deciding deadline into a required time column on {table} and use `expire at .expiresAt`, or filter the query (`{table} where {} …`); `expire at` accepts a local time column, not a reference hop", map_fields(&text, &|_, name| format!(".{name}"))),
        },
        "read" => format!("a read rule is an audience, which cannot compare magnitudes: filter the query instead (`{table} where {} …`)", map_fields(&text, &|_, name| format!(".{name}"))),
        _ => format!("check it in the mutation before the write: `row = {table}[id] ! else NOT_FOUND` then `require {} else {code}`", map_fields(&text, &stored)),
    };
    Diagnostic::new(site, "E_QUARRY_RULE_OPERATOR", message, rewrite).guide("rules")
}

/// An unnamed `update <- R` holds for the row before and after the write, so
/// its named form is `update (old, next) <- R(old) and R(next)`: every clause
/// kept, the ordered one included (lane 062). The mutation form follows.
pub(crate) fn named_update(table: &str, rule: &Expr, comparison: &str) -> String {
    let text = strip_parens(&crate::print::expression(rule));
    let wrap = |s: String| if text.contains(" or ") { format!("({s})") } else { s };
    let old = wrap(map_fields(&text, &|_, name| format!("old.{name}")));
    let next = wrap(map_fields(&text, &|_, name| format!("next.{name}")));
    let field = first_field(comparison).unwrap_or_else(|| "value".to_owned());
    let _ = table;
    format!("name both images; an unnamed update rule holds before and after the write, so the named form keeps both: `update (old, next) <- {old} and {next}`; or drop `{comparison}` from the rule and check the new value in the mutation: `require {} else INVALID_{}`", map_fields(comparison, &|_, name| name.to_owned()), screaming(&field))
}

/// Pasteable named form for a rule that already names one image. Bare focal
/// fields in a named transition refer to the new image.
pub(crate) fn named_update_source(rule: &Expr) -> String {
    // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#9 — preserve authored old/next images and map bare fields to next in named transitions.
    let text = crate::print::expression(rule);
    let body = map_fields(&text, &|image, name| match image {
        Some(image) => format!("{image}.{name}"),
        None => format!("next.{name}"),
    });
    format!("update (old, next) <- {body}")
}

/// A named transition's comparison the rule language cannot type, as the
/// mutation check that states the same condition.
pub(crate) fn transition_require(table: &str, cmp: &Expr) -> String {
    let text = strip_parens(&crate::print::expression(cmp));
    let field = first_field(&text).unwrap_or_else(|| "value".to_owned());
    let stored = |image: Option<&str>, name: &str| match image { Some("next") => name.to_owned(), _ => format!("row.{name}") };
    format!("check it in the mutation that updates the row: `row = {table}[id] ! else NOT_FOUND` then `require {} else INVALID_{}` (the new values are the mutation's arguments)", map_fields(&text, &stored), screaming(&field))
}

/// A table rule's predicate as the check a mutation states before writing:
/// the row's fields become the values the mutation writes.
pub(crate) fn mutation_check(rule: &Expr) -> String {
    map_fields(&strip_parens(&crate::print::expression(rule)), &|_, name| name.to_owned())
}

/// `else CODE` after a table rule: the refusal of a rule is E_RULE.
pub(crate) fn rule_else(else_site: &Site, effect: &str, rule: &Expr, code: &str) -> Diagnostic {
    let text = strip_parens(&crate::print::expression(rule));
    let code = if code.chars().next().is_some_and(|c| c.is_ascii_uppercase()) { code } else { "NOT_ALLOWED" };
    Diagnostic::new(else_site, "E_QUARRY_SYNTAX",
        format!("a table rule takes no `else`: a write its {effect} rule refuses is E_RULE; only `require … else CODE` and `unique … else CODE` name a refusal"),
        format!("keep `{effect} <- {text}`, and name the refusal in the mutation before the write: `require {} else {code}`", mutation_check(rule))).guide("rules")
}

fn strip_parens(text: &str) -> String {
    let trimmed = text.trim();
    if trimmed.starts_with('(') && trimmed.ends_with(')') {
        // Only strip a pair that encloses the whole text.
        let mut depth = 0i32;
        for (i, c) in trimmed.char_indices() {
            match c { '(' => depth += 1, ')' => depth -= 1, _ => {} }
            if depth == 0 && i + 1 < trimmed.len() { return trimmed.to_owned(); }
        }
        return trimmed[1..trimmed.len() - 1].to_owned();
    }
    trimmed.to_owned()
}

fn ident(c: char) -> bool { c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_' }
fn ident_start(c: char) -> bool { c.is_ascii_alphabetic() || c == '_' }

/// The first column the comparison names: `.stars`, `old.highBid` or `next.at`.
fn first_field(text: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
    for (i, c) in chars.iter().enumerate() {
        if *c == '.' && chars.get(i + 1).is_some_and(|c| ident_start(*c)) {
            return Some(chars[i + 1..].iter().take_while(|c| ident(**c)).collect());
        }
    }
    None
}

/// A time field owned by the focal row. Do not descend through a member
/// chain: `.hearing.releaseAt` must never become `expire at .hearing`.
fn direct_focal_field(expr: &Expr) -> Option<&str> {
    match expr {
        Expr::Member { base, name, .. } if matches!(base.as_ref(), Expr::Focal { .. }) => Some(name),
        Expr::Binary { left, right, .. } => direct_focal_field(left).or_else(|| direct_focal_field(right)),
        Expr::Unary { value, .. } => direct_focal_field(value),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Rewrite each focal field `.f`, `old.f` and `next.f` through `map(image, f)`,
/// leaving other member accesses alone.
fn map_fields(text: &str, map: &dyn Fn(Option<&str>, &str) -> String) -> String {
    let chars: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut i = 0;
    let name_at = |at: usize| -> String { chars[at..].iter().take_while(|c| ident(**c)).collect() };
    while i < chars.len() {
        let c = chars[i];
        // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#9 — field-looking text inside a literal is data, not a row-image reference.
        // Field-looking text inside a literal is data, not syntax. Preserve
        // the original spelling, including escaped quote characters.
        if matches!(c, '\'' | '"') {
            let quote = c;
            out.push(c);
            i += 1;
            while i < chars.len() {
                let literal = chars[i];
                out.push(literal);
                i += 1;
                if literal == '\\' && i < chars.len() {
                    out.push(chars[i]);
                    i += 1;
                } else if literal == quote {
                    break;
                }
            }
            continue;
        }
        let previous = if i == 0 { None } else { Some(chars[i - 1]) };
        if c == '.' && previous.is_none_or(|p| !ident(p) && p != ')' && p != ']') && chars.get(i + 1).is_some_and(|c| ident_start(*c)) {
            let name = name_at(i + 1);
            out.push_str(&map(None, &name));
            i += 1 + name.chars().count();
            continue;
        }
        if ident(c) && previous.is_none_or(|p| !ident(p) && p != '.') {
            let word = name_at(i);
            let after = i + word.chars().count();
            if matches!(word.as_str(), "old" | "next") && chars.get(after) == Some(&'.') && chars.get(after + 1).is_some_and(|c| ident_start(*c)) {
                let name = name_at(after + 1);
                out.push_str(&map(Some(&word), &name));
                i = after + 1 + name.chars().count();
                continue;
            }
            out.push_str(&word);
            i = after;
            continue;
        }
        out.push(c);
        i += 1;
    }
    out
}

fn screaming(name: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    for (i, c) in name.chars().enumerate() {
        if c.is_ascii_uppercase() && i > 0 { out.push('_'); }
        out.push(c.to_ascii_uppercase());
    }
    out
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn fields_move_into_the_mutation() {
        let stored = |image: Option<&str>, name: &str| match image { Some("next") => name.to_owned(), _ => format!("row.{name}") };
        assert_eq!(map_fields(".stars >= 1 and .stars <= 5", &|_, name| name.to_owned()), "stars >= 1 and stars <= 5");
        assert_eq!(map_fields("next.highBid >= old.highBid + old.increment", &stored), "highBid >= row.highBid + row.increment");
        assert_eq!(map_fields(".deadline > now", &stored), "row.deadline > now");
        assert_eq!(map_fields("helper(.a, viewer)", &stored), "helper(row.a, viewer)");
        assert_eq!(first_field("(old.highBid + 1)"), Some("highBid".into()));

//! Quarry text from syntax, for source-aware diagnostics and pasteable rewrites.
use crate::ast::*;

type Source<'a> = dyn Fn(&Expr) -> Option<(String, bool)> + 'a;

/// Rewrite callers may embed an expression in another operator or clause.
/// Use the same precedence renderer as source excerpts, with a grouped root.
pub fn expression(expr: &Expr) -> String {
    let grouped = match expr {
        Expr::Binary { .. } | Expr::Unary { .. } | Expr::If { .. } => true,
        Expr::Read(read) | Expr::Exists { read, .. } | Expr::Created { read, .. } =>
            read.filter.is_some() || read.matching.is_some() || read.range.is_some(),
        _ => false,
    };
    with_source_at(expr, if grouped { 8 } else { 0 }, &|_| None)
}

pub(crate) fn with_source(expr: &Expr, source: &Source<'_>) -> String { with_source_at(expr, 0, source) }
pub(crate) fn with_source_at(expr: &Expr, minimum: u8, source: &Source<'_>) -> String { render(expr, minimum, source) }

pub fn quote(value: &str) -> String {
    format!("'{}'", value.replace('\\', "\\\\").replace('\'', "\\'").replace('\n', "\\n").replace('\t', "\\t"))
}

fn priority(expr: &Expr) -> u8 {
    match expr {
        Expr::Binary { op, .. } => crate::parser::precedence(op).unwrap_or(0),
        Expr::If { .. } | Expr::Read(_) | Expr::Exists { .. } | Expr::Created { .. } | Expr::Merge(_) | Expr::Write { .. } | Expr::Walk { .. } => 0,
        Expr::Unary { .. } => 7,
        Expr::Assert { .. } | Expr::Shape { .. } | Expr::ShapeUse { .. } | Expr::Member { .. } => 8,
        _ => 9,
    }
}

fn render(expr: &Expr, minimum: u8, source: &Source<'_>) -> String {
    let wrap = |text: String, grouped: bool| if priority(expr) < minimum && !grouped { format!("({text})") } else { text };
    if let Some((text, grouped)) = source(expr) { return wrap(text, grouped); }
    let sub = |e| render(e, 0, source);
    let text = match expr {
        Expr::Name { name, .. } => name.clone(),
        Expr::Focal { .. } => ".".into(),
        Expr::Literal { value, .. } => match value {
            Literal::Str(s) => quote(s), Literal::Number(n) => n.clone(),
            Literal::Bool(b) => b.to_string(), Literal::Null => "null".into(),
        },
        Expr::Array { items, .. } => format!("[{}]", items.iter().map(sub).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")),
        Expr::Object { fields, .. } => format!("{{ {} }}", object_fields(fields, source)),
        Expr::Unary { op, value, .. } => {
            let value = render(value, 7, source);
            if op == "not" { format!("not {value}") }
            else if value.starts_with('-') { format!("-({value})") } else { format!("-{value}") }
        }
        Expr::Binary { op, left, right, .. } => {
            let p = priority(expr);
            let (l, r) = if op == "??" { (p + 1, p) } else { (p, p + 1) };
            format!("{} {op} {}", render(left, l, source), render(right, r, source))
        }
        Expr::Member { base, name, .. } => match base.as_ref() {
            Expr::Focal { .. } => format!(".{name}"),
            other => format!("{}.{name}", render(other, 8, source)),
        },
        Expr::Call { name, args, .. } => format!("{name}({})", args.iter().enumerate().map(|(n, arg)| {
            let value = sub(arg);
            if n > 0 && matches!(name.as_str(), "day" | "hour" | "bucket") && matches!(arg, Expr::Literal { value: Literal::Number(_), .. }) && source(arg).is_none() { format!("{value}ms") }
            else { value }
        }).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")),
        Expr::Read(read) => read_with(read, source),
        Expr::Merge(merge) => format!("merge {}{}{} {} {} by {}{}:", merge.table, merge.matching.as_ref().map_or(String::new(), |q| format!(" matching {}", sub(q))), merge.cursor.as_ref().map_or(String::new(), |c| format!(" after {}", sub(c))), if merge.order == Order::Asc { "first" } else { "last" }, merge.take, merge.index, merge.filter.as_ref().map_or(String::new(), |p| format!(" where {}", sub(p)))),
        Expr::Exists { read, .. } => format!("exists {}", read_with(read, source)),
        Expr::Created { read, .. } => format!("created {}", read_with(read, source)),
        Expr::Assert { value, code, message, .. } => format!("{} ! else {code}{}", render(value, 8, source), message.as_deref().map(|m| format!(" {}", quote(m))).unwrap_or_default()),
        Expr::ShapeUse { base, name, .. } => format!("{} {name}", render(base, 8, source)),
        Expr::Shape { base, fields, .. } => format!("{} {{ {} }}", render(base, 8, source), shape_with(fields, source)),
        Expr::Walk { table, seed, column, depth, .. } => format!("walk {table}[{}] up .{column} depth {depth}", sub(seed)),
        Expr::If { then, condition, otherwise, .. } => format!("{} if {} else {}", render(then, 1, source), render(condition, 1, source), sub(otherwise)),
        Expr::Write { op, table, keys, fields, if_absent, condition, .. } => {
            let mut out = format!("{} {table}", op.word());
            // `delete row` / `update row { … }` keep their row-variable spelling.
            if *op != WriteOp::Insert && !keys.is_empty() { out.push_str(&format!("[{}]", keys.iter().map(|k| key_part(k, source)).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "))); }
            if *op != WriteOp::Delete { out.push_str(&format!(" {{ {} }}", object_fields(fields, source))); }
            if *if_absent { out.push_str(" if absent"); }
            if let Some(condition) = condition { out.push_str(&format!(" if {}", sub(condition))); }
            out
        }
    };
    wrap(text, false)
}

pub fn read_expr(read: &ReadExpr) -> String { read_with(read, &|_| None) }

fn read_with(read: &ReadExpr, source: &Source<'_>) -> String {
    if let Some((text, _)) = source(&Expr::Read(read.clone())) { return text; }
    let sub = |e| render(e, 0, source);
    if !read.order_keys.is_empty() && read.keys.iter().all(|key| key.column.is_some()) {
        let mut predicates = read.keys.iter().map(|key| format!(".{} = {}", key.column.as_ref().unwrap(), render(&key.value, 5, source))).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        predicates.extend(read.seeks.iter().map(|bound| format!(".{} {} {}", bound.column, bound.op, render(&bound.value, 5, source))));
        if let Some(filter) = &read.filter { predicates.push(render(filter, if predicates.is_empty() { 0 } else { 3 }, source)); }
        let mut out = read.table.clone();
        if !predicates.is_empty() { out.push_str(&format!(" where {}", predicates.join(" and "))); }
        if let Some(matching) = &read.matching { out.push_str(&format!(" matching {}", sub(matching))); }
        if let Some(range) = &read.range { out.push_str(&format!(" {} {}", if range.order == Order::Asc { "first" } else { "last" }, range.take)); }
        out.push_str(&format!(" by {}", read.order_keys.iter().map(|key| format!(".{key}")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")));
        if let Some(cursor) = read.range.as_ref().and_then(|range| range.cursor.as_ref()) { out.push_str(&format!(" after {}", sub(cursor))); }
        return out;
    }
    let mut out = format!("{}[{}]", read.table, read.keys.iter().map(|key| key_part(key, source)).chain(read.seeks.iter().map(|b| format!("{} {} {}", b.column, b.op, sub(&b.value)))).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "));
    if let Some(matching) = &read.matching { out.push_str(&format!(" matching {}", sub(matching))); }
    if let Some(range) = &read.range {
        if let Some(cursor) = &range.cursor { out.push_str(&format!(" after {}", sub(cursor))); }
        out.push_str(&format!(" {} {}", if range.order == Order::Asc { "first" } else { "last" }, range.take));
    }
    if let Some(index) = &read.index { out.push_str(&format!(" by {index}")); }
    if let Some(filter) = &read.filter { out.push_str(&format!(" where {}", sub(filter))); }
    out
}

fn key_part(part: &KeyPart, source: &Source<'_>) -> String {
    let value = render(&part.value, 0, source);
    match &part.column { Some(column) => format!("{column} = {value}"), None => value }
}

fn object_fields(fields: &[ObjectField], source: &Source<'_>) -> String {
    fields.iter().map(|field| match &field.value {
        Some(value) if field.spread => format!("...{}", render(value, 8, source)),
        Some(value) => format!("{}: {}", field.name, render(value, 0, source)), None => field.name.clone(),
    }).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
}

fn shape_with(fields: &[ShapeField], source: &Source<'_>) -> String {
    fields.iter().map(|field| match field {
        ShapeField::Spread { .. } => "*".to_owned(), ShapeField::NamedSpread { name, .. } => format!("...{name}"),
        ShapeField::Bare { name, .. } => name.clone(),
        ShapeField::Field { name, value, .. } => format!("{name}: {}", render(value, 0, source)),
    }).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")
}

pub fn scalar_type(type_: &ScalarType) -> String {
    let base = match &type_.kind {
        TypeKind::Cursor => "cursor".to_owned(),
        TypeKind::Text { min, max, format } => {
            let mut out = match min {
                Some(min) => format!("text {min}..{max}"),
                None => format!("text <={max}"),
            };
            if let Some(format) = format {
                out.push_str(&format!(" format {format}"));
            }
            out
        }
        TypeKind::Id => "id".into(),
        TypeKind::Principal => "principal".into(),
        TypeKind::Int => "int".into(),
        TypeKind::IntRange { min, max } => snapback4_core::schema::int_range_text(*min, *max),
        TypeKind::Decimal { scale } => format!("decimal {scale}"),
        TypeKind::Money { currency, scale } => format!("money {currency} {scale}"),
        TypeKind::Time => "time".into(),
        TypeKind::Bool => "bool".into(),
        TypeKind::Json { max } => format!("json <={max}"),
        TypeKind::Bytes { max } => format!("bytes <={max}"),
        TypeKind::Image { max, once } => format!("image <={max}{}", if *once { " once" } else { "" }),
        TypeKind::Video { max } => format!("video <={max}"),
        TypeKind::File { max, types } if types.is_empty() => format!("file <={max}"),
        TypeKind::File { max, types } => format!("file <={max} ({})", types.iter().map(|t| format!("'{t}'")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")),
        TypeKind::Enum { variants } => format!("enum({})", variants.iter().map(|v| format!("'{v}'")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")),
        TypeKind::Ref { table } => table.clone(),
        TypeKind::List { item, min: 0, max } => format!("[{}] <={max}", scalar_type(item)),
        TypeKind::List { item, min, max } => format!("[{}] {min}..{max}", scalar_type(item)),
    };
    if type_.optional { format!("{base} ?") } else { base }
}

//! Calibration 23: repair expiry-scan admission first; retain the receipt-gap fallback.
use snapback4_core::{Context, Engine, Store, Value, WriteState};
use snapback4_lang::{compile, guide};

fn recipe() -> String {
    guide::quarry(guide::card("sequences").unwrap()).into_iter()
        .find(|s| s.contains("mutation skipExpiredBefore")).unwrap()
}
fn checked(s: &str) -> snapback4_lang::Bound {
    let b = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), s.into())]);
    assert!(b.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
    assert!(b.notes.is_empty(), "{:?}", b.notes);
    b
}
fn id(s: &str) -> Value { Value::Id(s.into()) }
fn write(e: &mut Engine, op: &str, args: &[(&str, Value)], ids: &[&str], now: i64) -> Value {
    let ctx = Context::new("alice", args.iter().map(|(k,v)| (k.to_string(), v.clone())).collect())
        .with_ids(ids.iter().map(|s| s.to_string())).at(now);
    match e.mutate(op, None, ctx).unwrap().state {
        WriteState::Sent { result, .. } => result,
        state => panic!("{op}: {state:?}"),
    }
}

#[test]
fn diary_and_run_log_intents_reach_the_recipe_directly() {
    for phrase in ["receipt gap expiring messages", "receipt gap", "receipt gaps", "expiring messages",
        "skip expired gaps in receipts", "advance delivered prefix over expired messages",
        "resume receipts after messages expire", "move receipt watermark past expired messages",
        "disappearing message receipt", "Bounded unique ordinal probes", "SEQUENCES",
        "what did this member miss", "bounded unique ordinal probes", "expired ordinal holes",
        "mutation page over expiring messages", "prohibited mutation scan over expiring rows", "sequence by"] {
        assert_eq!(guide::card(phrase), guide::card("sequences"), "{phrase}");
    }
    checked(&recipe());
    assert!(guide::explain_code("E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT").unwrap().contains("sequence by conversationId"));
}

#[test]
fn sequences_card_leads_with_admitted_receipt_reads_and_runtime_backlog_bounds() {
    let card = guide::card("receipt gap expiring messages").unwrap();
    assert!(card.contains("reads the first live blocker before deleting runs or writing"));
    assert!(card.contains("mutation delivered(conversationId: conversations, from: int, through: int): server"));
    assert!(card.find("mutation delivered(").unwrap() < card.find("fn skipExpired_messages").unwrap());
    assert!(card.contains("the ceiling refuses `E_BOUND` atomically"));
    assert!(card.contains("For shapes still refused"));
    assert!(!card.contains("E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT refuses a mutation page over expiring messages"));
}

fn refused_gap(keys: &str) -> String {
    let scan_index = if keys.contains("conversation, ordinal") { "" } else { "  by byConversationOrdinal: conversation, ordinal, id\n" };
    format!("table conversations:\n  public\n  online only\ntable messages:\n  conversation: conversations\n  other: conversations\n  ordinal: int\n  externalNumber: int\n  expiresAt: time ?\n{keys}\n{scan_index}  public\n  expire at .expiresAt\n  online only\neffect observeGap\nmutation gap(conversation: conversations):\n  emit observeGap {{}}\n  return first(messages where .conversation = conversation and .ordinal > 0 first 1 by .ordinal)\n")
}

// @ref LLP 3000.025#3-proposed-rule — these scans now admit before effects; the receipt helper remains an alternative after the phase ends.
fn assert_initial_read_admitted(source: &str) {
    let source = source.replace("  emit observeGap {}\n", "");
    let b = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source)]);
    assert!(b.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
    assert_eq!(b.schema.operations["gap"].predicts.as_deref(), Some("never"));
}

#[test]
fn receipt_helper_keeps_the_source_boundary_repair_first() {
    let source = refused_gap("  unique conversation, ordinal");
    let b = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.clone())]);
    assert_eq!(b.diagnostics.len(), 1, "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
    let d = &b.diagnostics[0];
    assert_eq!(d.code, "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT");
    assert!(d.message.contains("after `emit observeGap`"), "{d}");
    let repair = d.rewrite.find("above the entire `emit observeGap`").expect(&d.rewrite);
    let helper = d.rewrite.find("fn skipExpired_messages").expect(&d.rewrite);
    assert!(repair < helper && d.rewrite.contains("Fallback"), "{d}");
    // Moving the scan ahead of the emit is sufficient; no helper is needed.
    checked(&source.replace("  emit observeGap {}\n  return first(", "  blocker = first(")
        .replace("first 1 by .ordinal)\n", "first 1 by .ordinal)\n  emit observeGap {}\n  return blocker\n"));
}

#[test]
fn receipt_helper_keeps_the_prediction_repair_first() {
    let source = refused_gap("  unique conversation, ordinal")
        .replace("  online only\n", "  sync public last 500 by .id\n")
        .replace("  emit observeGap {}\n", "")
        .replace("mutation gap(", "mutation inspect(");
    let b = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.clone())]);
    assert_eq!(b.diagnostics.len(), 1, "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
    let d = &b.diagnostics[0];
    assert_eq!(d.code, "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT");
    let repair = d.rewrite.find("Make `inspect` `: server`").expect(&d.rewrite);
    let helper = d.rewrite.find("fn skipExpired_messages").expect(&d.rewrite);
    assert!(repair < helper && d.rewrite.contains("Fallback"), "{d}");
    assert!(!d.rewrite.contains("Move this scan"), "no effect ends this prefix: {d}");
    let repaired = checked(&source.replace("mutation inspect(conversation: conversations):", "mutation inspect(conversation: conversations): server"));
    assert_eq!(repaired.schema.operations["inspect"].predicts.as_deref(), Some("never"));
}

#[test]
fn receipt_helper_keeps_both_prediction_and_source_boundary_repairs() {
    let source = refused_gap("  unique conversation, ordinal")
        .replace("  online only\n", "  sync public last 500 by .id\n");
    let b = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.clone())]);
    assert_eq!(b.diagnostics.len(), 1, "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
    let d = &b.diagnostics[0];
    assert_eq!(d.code, "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT");
    let prediction = d.rewrite.find("Make `gap` `: server`").expect(&d.rewrite);
    let boundary = d.rewrite.find("above the entire `emit observeGap`").expect(&d.rewrite);
    let helper = d.rewrite.find("fn skipExpired_messages").expect(&d.rewrite);
    assert!(prediction < boundary && boundary < helper, "{d}");
    checked(&source.replace("mutation gap(conversation: conversations):", "mutation gap(conversation: conversations): server")
        .replace("  emit observeGap {}\n  return first(", "  blocker = first(")
        .replace("first 1 by .ordinal)\n", "first 1 by .ordinal)\n  emit observeGap {}\n  return blocker\n"));
}

#[test]
fn helper_follows_the_scan_coordinate_regardless_of_key_order_or_other_indexes() {
    for keys in [
        "  unique aExternal: conversation, externalNumber\n  unique zOrdinal: conversation, ordinal",
        "  unique reversed: ordinal, conversation",
        "  unique aOther: other, ordinal\n  unique zOrdinal: conversation, ordinal",
        "  unique aOther: other, externalNumber\n  unique zOrdinal: conversation, ordinal",
    ] {
        let source = refused_gap(keys);
        assert_initial_read_admitted(&source);
        let b = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.clone())]);
        let d = b.diagnostics.iter().find(|d| d.code == "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT").unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{:?}", b.diagnostics));
        assert!(d.rewrite.contains("conversation = scope, ordinal = prefix + 1"), "{keys}: {d}");
        let schema = source.split("mutation gap").next().unwrap();
        let repaired = checked(&format!("{schema}\n{}\nmutation gap(conversation: conversations):\n  return skipExpired_messages(conversation, 0, 4)\n", d.rewrite));
        let mut e = Engine::memory(repaired.schema, repaired.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
        for (name, ordinal, external) in [("one", 1, 100), ("four", 4, 400)] {
            e.seed_at([("messages".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
                ("id", id(name)), ("conversation", id("chat")), ("other", id("other")),
                ("ordinal", Value::Int(ordinal)), ("externalNumber", Value::Int(external)),
                ("expiresAt", Value::Null),
            ]))], 1).unwrap();
        }
        assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "gap", &[("conversation", id("chat"))], &[], 2), Value::Int(0), "{keys}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn deny_and_read_through_scopes_require_authority_before_using_the_prefix() {
    for read in ["read <- deny", "read through .conversation"] {
        let source = refused_gap("  unique conversation, ordinal")
            .replace("  conversation: conversations\n", "  conversation: conversations\n  immutable conversation\n")
            .replace("  public\n  expire", &format!("  {read}\n  expire"))
            .replace("table conversations:\n  public", "table conversations:\n  read <- deny");
        assert_initial_read_admitted(&source);
        let b = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.clone())]);
        let d = b.diagnostics.iter().find(|d| d.code == "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT").unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{:?}", b.diagnostics));
        assert!(d.rewrite.contains("skipExpired"), "{read}: {d}");
        assert!(d.message.contains("prefix justifies advancing a receipt only after the caller's own authority check"), "{read}: {d}");
        let schema = source.split("mutation gap").next().unwrap();
        let b = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!("{schema}\n{}\nmutation gap(conversation: conversations):\n  anchor = messages[conversation = conversation, ordinal = 3] ! else NOT_FOUND\n  return skipExpired_messages(conversation, 0, 3)\n", d.rewrite))]);
        assert!(b.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
        assert_eq!(b.notes.len(), 1, "{:?}", b.notes);
        assert_eq!(b.notes[0].code, "N_UNREADABLE_PROBE");
        assert!(b.notes[0].message.contains("negative guard"));
        let mut e = Engine::memory(b.schema, b.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
        use snapback4_core::value::object;
        e.seed_at([("conversations".into(), object([("id", id("chat"))]))], 1).unwrap();
        for occupied in [false, true] {
            if occupied {
                e.seed_at([("messages".into(), object([
                    ("id", id("hidden")), ("conversation", id("chat")), ("other", id("chat")),
                    ("ordinal", Value::Int(3)), ("externalNumber", Value::Int(50)), ("expiresAt", Value::Null),
                ]))], 1).unwrap();
            }
            let r = e.mutate("gap", None, Context::new("alice", [("conversation".into(), id("chat"))].into()).at(2)).unwrap();
            assert!(matches!(r.state, WriteState::Failed { .. }), "{read}, occupied={occupied}: {r:?}");
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn no_unique_key_covering_the_scan_coordinate_withholds_the_helper() {
    let source = refused_gap("  unique aExternal: conversation, externalNumber");

#[test]
fn uniform_membership_rule_still_requires_the_callers_authority_check() {
    let source = refused_gap("  unique conversation, ordinal")
        .replace("table messages:", "table members:\n  conversation: conversations\n  principal: principal\n  unique conversation, principal\n  public\n  online only\ntable messages:")
        .replace("  public\n  expire", "  read <- exists members[.conversation, viewer]\n  expire");
    assert_initial_read_admitted(&source);
    let b = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.clone())]);
    let d = b.diagnostics.iter().find(|d| d.code == "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT").unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{:?}", b.diagnostics));
    assert!(d.rewrite.contains("skipExpired"), "uniformity alone is not caller authority");
    assert!(d.message.contains("prefix justifies advancing a receipt only after the caller's own authority check"), "{d}");
    assert!(guide::card("sequences").unwrap().contains("prefix justifies advancing a receipt only after the caller's own authority check"));
    // The safe integration explicitly checks membership. No membership means
    // refusal, whether a live hidden row occupies the gap or it is absent.
    let schema = source.split("mutation gap").next().unwrap();
    let b = checked(&format!("{schema}\n{}\nmutation gap(conversation: conversations):\n  require exists members[conversation, viewer] else NOT_MEMBER\n  return skipExpired_messages(conversation, 0, 3)\n", d.rewrite));
    let mut e = Engine::memory(b.schema, b.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
    for occupied in [false, true] {
        if occupied {
            e.seed_at([("messages".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
                ("id", id("hidden")), ("conversation", id("chat")), ("other", id("other")),
                ("ordinal", Value::Int(1)), ("externalNumber", Value::Int(100)), ("expiresAt", Value::Null),
            ]))], 1).unwrap();
        }
        let r = e.mutate("gap", None, Context::new("alice", [("conversation".into(), id("chat"))].into()).at(2)).unwrap();
        assert!(matches!(r.state, WriteState::Failed { .. }), "{r:?}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn expiry_page_refusal_supplies_a_pasteable_helper_for_both_allocators() {
    let source = recipe();
    let helper_start = source.find("fn skipExpired_messages").unwrap();
    let helper_end = source.find("mutation skipExpiredBefore").unwrap();
    let mut source = source[..helper_start].to_owned() + &source[helper_end..];
    source.replace_range(source.find("mutation delivered(").unwrap()..source.find("query whatDidIMiss").unwrap(), "");
    for manual in [false, true] {
        for (parent, ordinal) in [("conversationId", "ordinal"), ("room", "position")] {
            let source = source.replace("conversationId", parent).replace("ordinal", ordinal);
            let source = if manual { source.replace(&format!("{ordinal}: sequence by {parent}"), &format!("{ordinal}: int\n  immutable {parent}, {ordinal}"))
                .replace("sender: viewer, expiresAt", &format!("sender: viewer, {ordinal}: 1, expiresAt")) } else { source };
            // Minimal reproduction of the recorded first-live-message gap scan;
            // the supplied artifact copy does not contain the builder's rejected source.
            let refused = source.replace(&format!("prefix = skipExpired_messages(message.{parent}, prefix, message.{ordinal})"),
                &format!("gap = first(messages where .{parent} = message.{parent} and .{ordinal} > prefix first 1 by .{ordinal})"));
            let admitted = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), refused.clone())]);
            assert!(admitted.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", admitted.diagnostics);
            assert_eq!(admitted.schema.operations["skipExpiredBefore"].predicts.as_deref(), Some("never"));
            // LLP 3000.025 admits the original initial scan. An earlier emit
            // ends that phase; keep all helper-coordinate and authority checks.
            let refused = format!("effect observeGap\n{}", refused.replace("gap = first(messages", "emit observeGap {}\n  gap = first(messages"));
            let b = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), refused.clone())]);
            assert_eq!(b.diagnostics.len(), 1, "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
            let d = &b.diagnostics[0];
            assert_eq!(d.code, "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT");
            assert_eq!(d.guide, "sequences");
            assert!(!d.mechanical);
            assert!(d.message.contains(&format!("{ordinal}: sequence by {parent}")), "{d}");
            assert!(d.rewrite.contains(&format!("exists messages[{parent} = scope, {ordinal} = prefix + 1]")), "{d}");
            assert!(d.rewrite.contains("range(0, 1024)"));
            let repaired = format!("{source}\n{}\n", d.rewrite);
            checked(&repaired);
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn recipe_skips_expired_positions_but_never_live_messages_on_memory_and_sqlite() {
    for disk in [false, true] {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("receipt-gaps-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let path = dir.join("store.sqlite");
        let store = if disk { Store::open(&path).unwrap() } else { Store::memory().unwrap() };
        let b = checked(&recipe());
        let mut e = Engine::new(store, b.schema, b.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
        write(&mut e, "createConversation", &[], &["chat", "member"], 1);
        assert_eq!(e.store().rows("members").unwrap()[0].field("joinedAt").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
        for (name, expiry) in [("gone", Value::Int(10)), ("live", Value::Null), ("later", Value::Null)] {
            write(&mut e, "send", &[("conversationId", id("chat")), ("expiresAt", expiry)], &[name], 2);
        }
        assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "skipExpiredBefore", &[("next", id("later"))], &[], 9), Value::Int(1));
        assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "skipExpiredBefore", &[("next", id("later"))], &[], 10), Value::Int(2));
        assert_eq!(e.store().rows("messages").unwrap().len(), 3, "expiry works before physical sweep");
        assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "skipExpiredBefore", &[("next", id("live"))], &[], 10), Value::Int(2));
        // A second member shares the same counter. Seed is a trusted fixture import.
        e.seed([("members".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
            ("id", id("bob-member")), ("conversationId", id("chat")), ("principal", id("bob")),
            ("deliveredOrdinal", Value::Int(0)),
        ]))]).unwrap();
        write(&mut e, "send", &[("conversationId", id("chat")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(20))], &["new"], 11);
        let count = |e: &mut Engine, now| e.query("whatDidIMiss", Context::new("bob", [("member".into(), id("bob-member"))].into()).at(now)).unwrap();
        let before = count(&mut e, 19);
        let after = count(&mut e, 20);
        assert!(before.complete && after.complete);
        assert_eq!(before.data, Value::Int(1));
        assert_eq!(after.data, Value::Int(0));
        drop(e);
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir).unwrap();
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_uniform_sender_page_does_not_justify_treating_other_senders_as_holes() {
    let source = "table conversations:\n  public\n  online only\ntable messages:\n  conversation: conversations\n  ordinal: int\n  sender: principal\n  expiresAt: time ?\n  unique conversation, ordinal\n  read <- .sender = viewer\n  expire at .expiresAt\n  online only\neffect observeGap\nmutation gap(conversation: conversations):\n  emit observeGap {}\n  return first(messages where .conversation = conversation and .sender = viewer first 1 by .ordinal)\n";
    assert_initial_read_admitted(source);
    let b = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
    let d = b.diagnostics.iter().find(|d| d.code == "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT").expect("expiry page refused");
    assert!(!d.rewrite.contains("skipExpired"), "a hidden message is not an expired hole: {d}");
    assert!(d.message.contains("after `emit observeGap`"), "{d}");
    assert!(d.rewrite.contains("entire `emit observeGap`"), "{d}");
    assert!(!d.rewrite.contains("selected ids"), "{d}");
}

#[test]
fn integrated_delivered_run_merge_resumes_a_repeated_receipt_in_the_builder() {
    for probes in [false, true] {
        integrated_delivered_run_merge(probes);
    }
}

fn integrated_delivered_run_merge(probes: bool) {
    let root = std::path::Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
        .join("../../../benchmarks/runs/2026-09-27-snapback4-clique-astra-0.4.4/astra/source/snapback");
    let mut docs: Vec<_> = std::fs::read_dir(root).unwrap().map(|entry| entry.unwrap().path())
        .filter(|path| path.extension().is_some_and(|ext| ext == "q")).map(|path| {
        (path.file_name().unwrap().to_str().unwrap().to_owned(), std::fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap())
    }).collect();
    docs.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));
    let card = recipe();
    let helper = card.split("fn skipExpired_messages").nth(1).unwrap().split("mutation skipExpiredBefore").next().unwrap();
    let delivered = card.split("mutation delivered").nth(1).unwrap().split("query whatDidIMiss").next().unwrap();
    let delivered = if probes {
        let start = delivered.find("  if prefix + 1 < low:").unwrap();
        let end = delivered[start..].find("  for run in held:").unwrap() + start;
        let mut delivered = delivered.to_owned();
        delivered.replace_range(start..end, "  prefix = skipExpired_messages(conversationId, prefix, low)\n");
        delivered
    } else { delivered.to_owned() };
    let integrated = format!("fn skipExpired_messages{helper}\nmutation delivered{delivered}\n")
        .replace("conversationId", "conversation").replace("joinedAt", "joinedOrdinal")
        .replace("conversation = conversations[conversation] ! else NOT_FOUND", "chat = conversations[conversation] ! else NOT_FOUND")
        .replace("conversation: conversation.id", "conversation: chat.id");
    let (_, messaging) = docs.iter_mut().find(|(name, _)| name == "messaging.q").unwrap();
    let start = messaging.find("mutation delivered(").unwrap();
    let end = messaging.find("mutation seen(").unwrap();
    messaging.replace_range(start..end, &integrated);
    let b = compile(&docs);
    assert!(b.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
    assert_eq!(b.schema.operations["messaging.delivered"].predicts.as_deref(), Some("never"));
    let mut e = Engine::memory(b.schema, b.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
    use snapback4_core::value::object;
    e.seed_at([
        ("conversations".into(), object([("id", id("chat")), ("creatorId", id("alice")), ("kind", Value::String("group".into())), ("lastOrdinal", Value::Int(1030))])),
        ("members".into(), object([("id", id("ma")), ("conversation", id("chat")), ("principal", id("alice")), ("role", Value::String("admin".into())), ("joinedOrdinal", Value::Int(0))])),
    ], 1).unwrap();
    e.seed_at([
        ("messages".into(), object([("id", id("received")), ("conversation", id("chat")), ("sender", id("bob")), ("ordinal", Value::Int(1027)), ("recipients", Value::Int(1)), ("text", Value::String("live anchor".into())), ("at", Value::Int(2))])),
        ("runs".into(), object([("id", id("disjoint")), ("conversation", id("chat")), ("principal", id("alice")), ("fromOrdinal", Value::Int(1030)), ("throughOrdinal", Value::Int(1030))])),
    ], 2).unwrap();
    let args = [("conversation", id("chat")), ("from", Value::Int(1027)), ("through", Value::Int(1027))];
    for (expected, runs) in [if probes { (1024, 2) } else { (1027, 1) }, (1027, 1), (1027, 1)] {
        write(&mut e, "messaging.delivered", &args, &[], 3);
        assert_eq!(e.store().rows("members").unwrap()[0].field("deliveredOrdinal").unwrap(), &Value::Int(expected));
        let held = e.store().rows("runs").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(held.len(), runs);
        assert!(held.iter().any(|row| row.field("id").unwrap() == &id("disjoint")));
    }
}

#[test]
fn server_receipt_scan_stops_at_live_blockers_then_resumes_the_saved_run() {
    let b = checked(&recipe());
    assert_eq!(b.schema.operations["delivered"].predicts.as_deref(), Some("never"));
    let mut e = Engine::memory(b.schema, b.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
    write(&mut e, "createConversation", &[], &["chat", "member"], 1);
    for (name, expiry) in [("gone", Value::Int(10)), ("blocker", Value::Int(20)), ("received", Value::Null)] {
        write(&mut e, "send", &[("conversationId", id("chat")), ("expiresAt", expiry)], &[name], 2);
    }
    let args = [("conversationId", id("chat")), ("from", Value::Int(4)), ("through", Value::Int(4))];
    assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "delivered", &args, &["held"], 10), Value::Int(2));
    let runs = e.store().rows("runs").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(runs.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(runs[0].field("fromOrdinal").unwrap(), &Value::Int(4));
    assert_eq!(write(&mut e, "delivered", &args, &[], 20), Value::Int(4));
    assert!(e.store().rows("runs").unwrap().is_empty());
    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("messages").unwrap().len(), 3, "no physical sweep needed");
}

// @ref LLP 3000.025#3-proposed-rule — full slots must refuse without claiming coverage, then recover on a fresh id.
#[test]
fn card_full_slots_refuse_runs_full_roll_back_and_recover() {
    use snapback4_core::value::object;
    let source = format!("{}\nmutation freeSlot(): server\n  delete runs['r0']\n", recipe());
    let b = checked(&source);
    let mut e = Engine::memory(b.schema, b.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
    write(&mut e, "createConversation", &[], &["c", "member"], 1);
    for (name, expiry) in [("gone", Value::Int(10)), ("blocker", Value::Null), ("received", Value::Null)] {
        write(&mut e, "send", &[("conversationId", id("c")), ("expiresAt", expiry)], &[name], 2);
    }
    e.seed_at((0..64).map(|n| ("runs".into(), object([
        ("id", id(&format!("r{n}"))), ("conversationId", id("c")), ("principal", id("alice")),
        ("fromOrdinal", Value::Int(10 + 2 * n)), ("throughOrdinal", Value::Int(10 + 2 * n)),
    ]))), 2).unwrap();
    let tables = ["conversations", "members", "messages", "runs"];
    let before = tables.map(|table| e.store().rows(table).unwrap());
    let seq = e.store().seq().unwrap();
    let ctx = || Context::new("alice", [
        ("conversationId".into(), id("c")), ("from".into(), Value::Int(4)), ("through".into(), Value::Int(4)),
    ].into()).with_ids(["received-run".to_owned()]).at(10);
    let full = e.mutate("delivered", Some("full"), ctx()).unwrap();
    assert!(matches!(&full.state, WriteState::Failed { why, .. } if why.code == "RUNS_FULL"), "{:?}", full.state);
    assert_eq!(tables.map(|table| e.store().rows(table).unwrap()), before, "refusal must leave every application row unchanged");
    assert_eq!(e.store().seq().unwrap(), seq, "refusal must not publish a row change");
    write(&mut e, "freeSlot", &[], &[], 10);
    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("runs").unwrap().len(), 63);
    let replay = e.mutate("delivered", Some("full"), ctx()).unwrap();
    assert!(replay.replayed);
    assert_eq!(full.receipt(Some("full")), replay.receipt(Some("full")));
    let recovered = e.mutate("delivered", Some("recovered"), ctx()).unwrap();
    assert!(!recovered.replayed);
    assert!(matches!(&recovered.state, WriteState::Sent { result, .. } if result == &Value::Int(2)), "{:?}", recovered.state);
    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("members").unwrap()[0].field("deliveredOrdinal"), Ok(&Value::Int(2)));
    let runs = e.store().rows("runs").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(runs.len(), 64);
    assert!(runs.iter().any(|row| row.field("id") == Ok(&id("received-run"))
        && row.field("fromOrdinal") == Ok(&Value::Int(4)) && row.field("throughOrdinal") == Ok(&Value::Int(4))));
    for run in before[3].iter().filter(|row| row.field("id") != Ok(&id("r0"))) {
        assert!(runs.contains(run), "the other saved intervals must survive");
    }
    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("messages").unwrap(), before[2], "no physical sweep needed");
}

//! The catalog: every table (declared or generated for a maintain) with its
//! columns and indexes, plus the named shapes and functions, and where each
//! schema path was declared so a core validation issue can point at a line.

use crate::ast::*;
use crate::diag::{Diagnostic, Site, name_rewrite, unknown};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct TableInfo {
    pub through: Option<snapback4_core::schema::through::Through>,
    pub captures: BTreeMap<String, ScalarType>,
    pub recorded: BTreeMap<String, ScalarType>,
    pub decl: TableDecl,
    pub columns: BTreeMap<String, ScalarType>,
    pub indexes: Vec<IndexDecl>,
    /// Set when the table is a maintain's generated target.
    pub maintained: Option<MaintainDecl>,
}

impl TableInfo {
    pub fn total_unique(&self, index: &IndexDecl) -> bool {
        index.unique && index.is_plain() && index.columns.iter().all(|column| column == "id" || self.columns.get(column).is_some_and(|ty| !ty.optional))
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.013#2.1 — a scan cursor carries declared components only;
    // uniqueness with a nullable component cannot resolve ties between nulls.
    pub fn total_cursor(&self, index: &IndexDecl) -> bool {
        index.columns.iter().any(|column| column == "id") || index.unique && index.words.is_none()
            && index.columns.iter().all(|column| match index.computed.get(column) {
                Some(expr) => super::time_indexes::key(&self.decl.name, &self.columns, column, expr).is_ok(),
                None => self.columns.get(column).is_some_and(|ty| !ty.optional),
            })
    }
}

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Catalog {
    pub ordinary_searches: Vec<String>,
    pub source: crate::source::SourceMap,
    pub feed_views: BTreeMap<String, super::feed_view::Plan>,
    pub extremum_domains: BTreeMap<String, ReadExpr>,
    pub read_origins: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    pub canonical_read_origins: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    pub view_reads: BTreeMap<String, crate::ast::MergeExpr>,
    pub view_types: BTreeMap<String, crate::types::Ty>,
    pub planner_notes: Vec<Diagnostic>,
    /// Exact cap declarations that would admit an otherwise fully verified
    /// owner-or-membership page, keyed by the read's source site.
    pub membership_cap_repairs: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    pub synthesized: std::collections::BTreeSet<(String, String)>,
    pub documents: Vec<Document>,
    pub tables: BTreeMap<String, TableInfo>,
    pub maintains: BTreeMap<String, MaintainDecl>,
    pub shapes: BTreeMap<String, ShapeDecl>,
    pub functions: BTreeMap<String, FunctionDecl>,
    pub effects: BTreeMap<String, String>,
}

impl Catalog {
    pub fn build(documents: Vec<Document>, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) -> Self {
        let mut tables: BTreeMap<String, TableInfo> = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut maintains = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut shapes: BTreeMap<String, ShapeDecl> = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut functions: BTreeMap<String, FunctionDecl> = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut effects = BTreeMap::new();
        let mut effect_sites: BTreeMap<String, Site> = BTreeMap::new();
        for doc in &documents {
            for table in &doc.tables {
                if tables.contains_key(&table.name) {
                    diagnostics.push(unknown(&table.site, format!("duplicate table {}", table.name), "rename one of the two tables"));
                    continue;
                }
                let mut columns = BTreeMap::new();
                let mut ok = true;
                for column in &table.columns {
                    if column.name == "id" {
                        diagnostics.push(unknown(&column.site, format!("table {} gets id implicitly; remove the id column", table.name), "delete this line"));
                        ok = false;
                        continue;
                    }
                    if columns.insert(column.name.clone(), column.type_.clone()).is_some() {
                        diagnostics.push(unknown(&column.site, format!("duplicate column {}.{}", table.name, column.name), "rename one of the two columns"));
                        ok = false;
                    }
                }
                for field in &table.search {
                    if !matches!(columns.get(field), Some(ScalarType { kind: TypeKind::Text { .. } | TypeKind::Enum { .. }, .. })) {
                        diagnostics.push(crate::diag::type_error(&table.site, format!("search {} requires a text or enum column on {}", field, table.name), format!("declare `{field}: text <=2000` or `{field}: enum('one', 'two')` before `search {field}`")).guide("search"));
                    }
                }
                let mut indexes = vec![IndexDecl { name: "byId".into(), columns: vec!["id".into()], unique: true, refusal: None, words: None, computed: BTreeMap::new(), site: table.site.clone() }];
                for index in &table.indexes {
                    if indexes.iter().any(|existing| existing.name == index.name) {
                        diagnostics.push(unknown(&index.site, format!("duplicate index {}.{}", table.name, index.name), "name one ordering explicitly"));
                        ok = false;
                        continue;
                    }
                    for column in &index.columns {
                        if index.computed.contains_key(column) { continue; }
                        if column != "id" && !columns.contains_key(column) {
                            diagnostics.push(crate::diag::type_error(&index.site, format!("index {}.{} names unknown column {column}", table.name, index.name), name_rewrite(column, columns.keys().map(String::as_str).chain(["id"]), None)));
                            ok = false;
                        }
                    }
                    for field in index.words.iter().flat_map(|(_, fields)| fields) {
                        match columns.get(field) {
                            Some(ScalarType { kind: TypeKind::Text { .. } | TypeKind::Enum { .. }, .. }) => {}
                            // The table stays in the catalog: one line is
                            // wrong, and its readers should hear about that
                            // line, not about a table that vanished.
                            Some(other) => diagnostics.push(crate::diag::type_error(&index.site, format!("index {}.{} tokenizes {field}, which is {}, not text or enum", table.name, index.name, crate::print::scalar_type(other)), format!("words(<a text or enum column of {}>)", table.name))),
                            None => diagnostics.push(crate::diag::type_error(&index.site, format!("index {}.{} tokenizes unknown column {field}", table.name, index.name), name_rewrite(field, columns.keys().map(String::as_str), None))),
                        }
                    }
                    for (name, expr) in &index.computed {
                        if let Err(error) = super::time_indexes::key(&table.name, &columns, name, expr) { diagnostics.push(error); }
                    }
                    indexes.push(index.clone());
                }
                let mut seen_effects = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
                for rule in &table.rules {
                    if !seen_effects.insert(rule.effect) {
                        if rule.effect == Effect::Read && table.rules.iter().any(|r| matches!(&r.value,Expr::Call{name,..} if name=="$readThrough")) {
                            diagnostics.push(Diagnostic::new(&rule.site,"E_READ_THROUGH",format!("{} declares another read rule beside read through",table.name),"keep read through as the whole read rule; put service grants on the parent").guide("rules"));
                        } else { diagnostics.push(unknown(&rule.site, format!("duplicate {} rule on {}", rule.effect.word(), table.name), "keep one rule per effect")); }
                        ok = false;
                    }
                }
                if ok {
                    let mut decl = table.clone();
                    // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#9 — rejected search metadata must not erase the usable table symbol.
                    // An invalid search field is a fault of that search line,
                    // not evidence that every later reference names an
                    // unknown table. Keep the usable table symbol and omit
                    // only search fields that could not be indexed.
                    decl.search.retain(|field| matches!(columns.get(field), Some(ScalarType { kind: TypeKind::Text { .. } | TypeKind::Enum { .. }, .. })));
                    // @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — catalog consumers see the same
                    // implicit immutability as runtime schema consumers.
                    for column in &table.columns {
                        if let Some(parent) = &column.sequence {
                            decl.immutable.push((vec![column.name.clone(), parent.clone()], column.site.clone()));
                        }
                    }
                    tables.insert(table.name.clone(), TableInfo { through: None, captures: BTreeMap::new(), recorded: BTreeMap::new(), decl, columns, indexes, maintained: None });
                }
            }
            for maintain in &doc.maintains {
                if tables.contains_key(&maintain.name) || maintains.contains_key(&maintain.name) {
                    diagnostics.push(unknown(&maintain.site, format!("maintain {} collides with a table of the same name", maintain.name), "rename the aggregate view"));
                    continue;
                }
                let mut maintain = maintain.clone();
                super::maintains::normalize_keys(&mut maintain);
                maintains.insert(maintain.name.clone(), maintain);
            }
            for shape in &doc.shapes {
                if let Some(first) = shapes.get(&shape.name) {
                    diagnostics.push(unknown(&shape.site, format!("duplicate shape {}; first declared at {}", shape.name, first.site), "rename one shape"));
                    continue;
                }
                shapes.insert(shape.name.clone(), shape.clone());
            }
            for function in &doc.functions {
                if let Some(first) = functions.get(&function.name) {
                    diagnostics.push(unknown(&function.site, format!("duplicate fn {}; first declared at {}", function.name, first.site), "rename one function"));
                    continue;
                }
                // @ref LLP 3000.040#12-surface — a bound belongs to a slot a value enters (a column or an operation's argument); a helper is inlined and has none.
                for param in &function.args {
                    if let Some((min, max)) = int_range_of(&param.type_) {
                        let range = snapback4_core::schema::int_range_text(min, max);
                        diagnostics.push(crate::diag::type_error(&param.site, format!("{}'s parameter {} cannot be {range}: a helper is inlined, so no value crosses a boundary where the bound is checked", function.name, param.name),
                            format!("declare `{}: int` and bound the operation's argument or the stored column as {range}", param.name)).guide("types"));
                    }
                }
                functions.insert(function.name.clone(), function.clone());
            }
            for effect in &doc.effects {
                if let Some(first) = effect_sites.get(&effect.name) {
                    diagnostics.push(unknown(&effect.site, format!("duplicate effect {}; first declared at {first}", effect.name), "rename one effect"));
                    continue;
                }
                effect_sites.insert(effect.name.clone(), effect.site.clone());
                effects.insert(effect.name.clone(), effect.module.clone());
            }
        }
        super::through::expand(&mut tables, diagnostics);
        for maintain in maintains.values_mut() { if let Some(source)=tables.get(&maintain.source) { super::maintains::inherited_keys(source,maintain); } }
        super::columns::resolve(&mut tables, diagnostics);
        super::columns::recorded(&mut tables, diagnostics);
        // Resolve every path against application declarations before generating any target.
        for maintain in maintains.values().filter(|m|m.row_key.is_none()) {
            match super::maintains::recorded_paths(&tables, maintain) {
                Ok(paths) => { if let Some(source) = tables.get_mut(&maintain.source) { source.recorded.extend(paths); } }
                Err(diagnostic) => diagnostics.push(diagnostic),
            }
        }
        // Generated maintain targets join the catalog as tables.
        let names: Vec<String> = maintains.keys().cloned().collect();
        for name in names {
            let maintain = maintains[&name].clone();
            let Some(mut source) = tables.get(&maintain.source).cloned() else {
                diagnostics.push(unknown(&maintain.site, format!("maintain names unknown source table {}", maintain.source), name_rewrite(&maintain.source, tables.keys().map(String::as_str), None)));
                continue;
            };
            source.columns.extend(source.recorded.clone());
            source.columns.extend(source.captures.clone());

                Ok(decl) => {
        let site = keyword.site.clone();
        let name = self.binding_name()?;
        self.take(":")?;
        let aggregate = self.word()?;
        if aggregate.value != "count" && aggregate.value != "sum" {
            return Err(unsupported(&aggregate.site, &format!("maintain {}", aggregate.value), "use maintain name: count table by columns, or maintain name: sum table of intColumn by columns"));

        let source = self.word()?.value;
        let mut column = None;
        if aggregate.value == "sum" && self.at("where") {
            // `sum t where … of .x`: count's clause order; a sum names its value first.
            let where_site = self.take("where")?.site;
            let start = self.position;
            while !self.at("of") && !self.at_kind(Kind::Newline) && !self.at_kind(Kind::Eof) { self.position += 1; }
            let predicate = (self.position > start).then(|| self.source_text(start, self.position));
            let of = if self.maybe("of") { self.maybe("."); self.word().ok().map(|t| t.value) } else { None };
            let rest_start = self.position;
            while !self.at_kind(Kind::Newline) && !self.at_kind(Kind::Eof) { self.position += 1; }
            let rest = if self.position > rest_start { self.source_text(rest_start, self.position) } else { "by …".to_owned() };
            return Err(syntax_with(&where_site, "a sum names its value before its filter: sum source of .column where predicate by keys",

        }
        if aggregate.value == "sum" {
            if self.at(".") || !self.at("of") {

                return Err(syntax_with(&aggregate.site, "a maintained sum spells its source and value separately: sum source of .column by .group", format!("{} {name}: sum {source} of .{column} by .group", keyword.value)).guide("totals"));

            self.maybe(".");
            column = Some(self.word()?.value);

        let grouped = self.maybe("by");

            Some((self.word()?.value, self.word()?.value))
        } else { None };
        let mut keys = Vec::new();
        let keys_start = self.position;

            Expr::Name { name, .. } | Expr::Call { name, .. } => name.clone(),

        let block = self.at_kind(Kind::Indent);

        let mut read = None;
        let mut reviewed_disclosure = None;
        let mut online_only = false;
        while block && !self.at_kind(Kind::Dedent) && !self.at_kind(Kind::Eof) {

            if self.at_kind(Kind::Dedent) {

                    // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#9 — reviewed disclosure is a non-empty audit annotation, not runtime authority.
                    self.take("reviewed")?;
                    let reason = self.take_kind(Kind::Str)?.value;
                    if reason.trim().is_empty() {
                        return Err(syntax_with(
                            &effect.site,
                            "a reviewed disclosure needs a concrete rationale",
                            "disclosure reviewed 'why this aggregate delta is an intended read channel'",
                        ));
                    }
                    self.newline()?;
                    if reviewed_disclosure.replace(reason).is_some() {
                        return Err(syntax_with(
                            &effect.site,
                            "duplicate reviewed disclosure",
                            "keep one disclosure reviewed 'rationale' line",
                        ));
                    }
                    return Ok(());
                }
                if effect.value == "readable" {
                    return Err(unsupported(&effect.site, "readable on a maintain", "read <- rule  -- a maintain has one rule; the engine delivers it to its source's audience"));
                }
                if effect.value == "sync" {
                    return Err(crate::bind::audience_diagnostics::sync_syntax(&name, &source, &effect.site));
                }
                if effect.value != "read" && effect.value != "public" {
                    return Err(syntax_with(&effect.site, format!("unknown maintain property {}", effect.value), "read <- rule"));
                }
                // @ref LLP 3000.007#23 — public has the same read authority on tables and aggregate views.
                let value = if effect.value == "public" {
                    if self.at_kind(Kind::Str) { self.take_kind(Kind::Str)?; }
                    Expr::Name { name: "allow".into(), site: effect.site.clone() }
                } else { self.parse_focal_rule_value(&effect.value, &effect.site)? };
                self.newline()?;
                if read.is_some() {
                    return Err(syntax_with(&effect.site, format!("maintain {name} has more than one read rule"), "keep one read <- rule"));
                }
                read = Some(RuleDecl { effect: Effect::Read, bindings: Vec::new(), value, site: effect.site.clone() });
                Ok(())
            })();
            if let Err(diagnostic) = result {
                self.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
                self.recover_line();
            }
        }
        if block { self.take_kind(Kind::Dedent)?; }
        Ok(MaintainDecl { row_key, filter, keys, indexes, name, aggregate: aggregate.value, source, column, by, read, reviewed_disclosure, online_only, site })
    }
