//! Mutation population admission. A page consumed as a whole group must
//! preserve one complete, uniformly readable, schema-capped population when
//! predicting. A never-predicting page pass still requires uniform visibility.
//! Provenance follows bindings and row shaping, never just the final loop
//! syntax. Runtime metering remains independent and aborts over-budget writes.
// @ref LLP 3000.003#implementation-follow-up — retained structural admission
use crate::engine::rules::scan_visibility;
use crate::error::RuntimeError;
use crate::ir::*;
use crate::schema::{Constraint, Schema};
use crate::value::Value;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
mod maintenance_types;

pub fn check_state_predicates(schema: &Schema, program: &Program) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    maintenance_types::check(schema, program).map_err(|message| RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_VIEW_KEY", message })
}

/// Compiler-only helper identities join every call site's parameters/results.
/// They are absent from serialized programs and confer no native permission.
pub fn check_state_predicate_scopes(schema: &Schema, scopes: &[(&Program, &BTreeMap<String, String>)]) -> Vec<(usize, String)> {
    maintenance_types::check_scopes(schema, scopes)
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Origin {
    Other,
    Empty,
    Page(Scan),
    Merge(Vec<Scan>),
    Unknown(Vec<Scan>),
}

impl Origin {
    fn scans(&self) -> Vec<Scan> {
        match self {
            Self::Page(scan) => vec![scan.clone()],
            Self::Merge(scans) | Self::Unknown(scans) => scans.clone(),
            _ => Vec::new(),
        }
    }
    fn population(&self) -> bool {
        !matches!(self, Self::Other | Self::Empty)
    }
    fn join(self, other: Self) -> Self {
        if self == other {
            return self;
        }
        if !self.population() && !other.population() {
            return Self::Other;
        }
        let mut scans = self.scans();
        for scan in other.scans() {
            if !scans.contains(&scan) {
                scans.push(scan);
            }
        }
        if matches!(self, Self::Merge(_)) || matches!(other, Self::Merge(_)) {
            Self::Merge(scans)
        } else {
            Self::Unknown(scans)
        }
    }
    fn transformed(self) -> Self {
        match self {
            Self::Page(scan) => Self::Unknown(vec![scan]),
            origin => origin,
        }
    }
}


#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Problem {
    pub code: &'static str,
    pub site: String,
    pub page_site: Option<String>,
    pub message: String,
    pub rewrite: String,
}

pub fn check(schema: &Schema, program: &Program) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    check_detail(schema, program).map_err(|problem| RuntimeError::Structural { code: problem.code, message: problem.message })
}

// @ref LLP 3000.007#20 — admission reports the author's population and bound; source locations stay beside the IR.
pub fn check_detail(schema: &Schema, program: &Program) -> Result<(), Problem> {
    check_detail_with_statements(schema, program, &[])
}

/// Source statement ends supplied by Quarry alongside its flattened IR. Empty
/// means each IR statement owns itself (serialized/hand-built programs). Grouping
/// can only shorten eligibility: every statement in each group is still checked.
// @ref LLP 3000.025#3-proposed-rule — hoisted setup belongs to its entire source statement.
pub fn check_detail_with_statements(schema: &Schema, program: &Program, statement_ends: &[usize]) -> Result<(), Problem> {
    maintenance_types::check(schema, program).map_err(|message| Problem {
        code: "E_VIEW_KEY", site: program.name.clone(), page_site: None, message,
        rewrite: "project the field you need first: value or member fields; project recountPending as data and check complete; use a separate variable for the row".into(),
    })?;
    let mut fact = schema.operations.get(&program.name).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
    crate::schema::ephemeral::execution(schema, program, &mut fact).map_err(|message| Problem {
        code: "E_QUARRY_EPHEMERAL", site: program.name.clone(), page_site: None,
        message, rewrite: "split durable work from ephemeral mutations and queries".into(),
    })?;
    for table in crate::ir::read_sites(program).into_iter().map(|s|s.table).chain(crate::ir::write_tables(program).into_iter().map(|(t,_)|t)) {
        if let Err(error) = schema.refuse_private(&table) {
            return Err(Problem { code: "E_MAINTAINED_COLUMN_PRIVATE", site: program.name.clone(), page_site: None,
                message: error.to_string(), rewrite: "read the parent row or write its source rows".into() });
        }
    }
    let (scans, has_merge) = crate::ir::read_structure(program);
    if program.kind == ProgramKind::Mutation {
        require_uniform_mutation_pages(schema, program, &scans)?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#17 — structural merges and every mutation page are checked, including bound pages in predicting mutations.
        if has_merge { return Err(fanout(scans.first().copied(), &program.name, "a merge is not a plain prefix scan", "read this merge in a query, then pass the selected ids to the mutation")); }
        // @ref LLP 3000.025#3-proposed-rule — an entire read-only statement prefix precedes every effect, including hidden and indirect writes.
        let (prefix_len, effect_end) = read_only_prefix(&program.body, statement_ends);
        let (prelude, _) = crate::ir::body_read_structure(&program.body[..prefix_len]);
        let never = schema.operations.get(&program.name).is_some_and(|fact| fact.predicts.as_deref() == Some("never"));
        for scan in &scans {
            // Identity, not a forgeable diagnostic site or structural equality.
            let in_prefix = prelude.iter().any(|before| std::ptr::eq(*before, *scan));
            if let Some(reason) = plain_prefix_problem(schema, scan) {
                return Err(fanout(Some(scan), &scan.site, &reason, "read this page in a query, then pass the selected ids to the mutation"));
            }
            if schema.table(&scan.table).is_some_and(|table| table.read_lifetime_sensitive()) && !(never && in_prefix) {
                return Err(expiry_problem(program, scan, prefix_len..effect_end, never, in_prefix));
            }
        }
        let nonuniform = scans.iter().find(|s| {
                schema.table(&s.table).and_then(|t| t.index(&s.index)).is_some() && !decided(schema, program, s)
            }).map(|s| (*s).clone());
        let mut bindings = BTreeMap::new();
        collect(&program.body, true, &mut bindings);
        let env = program.args.keys().map(|name| {
                (name.clone(), if bindings.contains_key(name) { Origin::Unknown(vec![]) } else { Origin::Other },
                )
            }).collect();
        let mut flow = Flow { schema, program, nonuniform, env, error: None, bindings };
        flow.statements(&program.body, &Origin::Other, true);
        if let Some(error) = flow.error { return Err(error); }
        if flow.nonuniform.is_some() && crate::ir::write_tables(program).iter().any(|(name, effect)| {
            *effect != "delete" && schema.table(name).is_some_and(|t| {
                            t.constraints.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Constraint::Cap { .. }))
                        })
        }) {
            return Err(fanout(flow.nonuniform.as_ref(), &program.name, "a non-uniform scan cannot share a mutation with a complete population or group cap check", "read this page in a query, then pass the selected ids to the mutation"));
        }
    }
    for scan in scans {
        if schema.table(&scan.table).and_then(|t| t.index(&scan.index)).is_none() {
            return Err(Problem { code: "E_UNBOUND_SCAN", site: scan.site.clone(), page_site: None, message: format!("missing scan table or index {}.{}", scan.table, scan.index), rewrite: "declare this table and index".into() });
        }
    }
    Ok(())
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.025#6-diagnostics-and-exact-documentation-changes — name the enclosing statement, not an inferred product invariant.
fn expiry_problem(program: &Program, scan: &Scan, boundary: std::ops::Range<usize>, never: bool, in_prefix: bool) -> Problem {
    let mut message = format!("{} scans expiring {}", program.name, scan.table);
    let mut rewrite = if never { String::new() } else { format!("Make `{}` `: server`. ", program.name) };
    if in_prefix {
        message.push_str(" but may predict");
    } else if let Some(statement) = program.body[boundary.clone()].last() {
        let group = &program.body[boundary.clone()];
        let (inside, _) = crate::ir::body_read_structure(group);
        let enclosing = inside.iter().any(|candidate| std::ptr::eq(*candidate, scan));
        let site = match statement {
            Stmt::If { .. } => "if".into(),
            Stmt::For { .. } => "for".into(),
            Stmt::Emit { effect, .. } => format!("emit {effect}"),
            Stmt::Const { name, .. } | Stmt::Let { name, .. } | Stmt::Assign { name, .. } if !name.starts_with('$') =>
            {
                format!("binding {name}")
            }
            Stmt::Update { table, .. } => format!("update {table}"),
            Stmt::Upsert { table, .. } => format!("upsert {table}"),
            Stmt::WriteTarget { target, upsert, .. } => format!("{} {}", if *upsert { "upsert" } else { "update" }, target.table),
            Stmt::Delete { table, .. } => format!("delete {table}"),
            Stmt::DeleteTarget { target } => format!("delete {}", target.table),
            Stmt::Insert { table, .. } | Stmt::InsertIfAbsent { table, .. } => {
                format!("insert {table}")
            }
            _ => format!("statement {}", boundary.start + 1),
        };
        let effect = if super::read_only::statements::<true>(group) { "an emit" } else { "a write" };
        message.push_str(&if enclosing {
            format!(" inside `{site}` containing {effect} (an untaken arm counts)")
        } else {
            format!(" after `{site}` containing {effect}, ending the read-only phase")
        });
        if enclosing && let Stmt::For { .. } = statement {
            let single = Program { body: vec![statement.clone()], ..program.clone() };
            let writes = crate::ir::write_tables(&single);
            let action = writes.first().map_or("…", |(_, kind)| *kind);
            rewrite.push_str(&format!("Bind before this entire loop: `page = {} …`; `for row in page: {action} …`.", scan.table));
        } else {
            rewrite.push_str(&format!("Move this scan into its own statement above the entire `{site}`. Then write."));
        }
    }
    Problem { code: "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT", site: scan.site.clone(), page_site: Some(scan.site.clone()), message, rewrite: rewrite.trim().into() }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.025#3-proposed-rule — expiry alone may pass the server read-only prefix; matching and merges keep their refusal.
fn plain_prefix_problem(schema: &Schema, scan: &Scan) -> Option<String> {
    let table = schema.table(&scan.table)?;
    if !table.index(&scan.index)?.is_plain() || scan.prefix.iter().any(|key| matches!(key, IndexKeyExpr::WordPrefix(_))) {
        Some("matching word scans expand hidden words before deciding visibility; read it in a query, or use a plain prefix scan".into())
    } else if scan.merge_site.is_some() {
        Some("a merge is not a plain prefix scan; read it in a query, or use a job chunk".into())
    } else { None }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.007#14 — ruling 17 (c): binding a page has the same abort channel as looping over it.
fn require_uniform_mutation_pages(schema: &Schema, program: &Program, scans: &[&Scan]) -> Result<(), Problem> {
    for scan in scans {
        if schema.table(&scan.table).and_then(|table| table.index(&scan.index)).is_some() && !decided(schema, program, scan) {
            return Err(fanout(Some(scan), &scan.site, "the mutation page's read rule is not uniformly decided by its prefix", &uniform_rewrite(schema, scan)));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// The page's verdict is one for every row: its prefix decides the read rule,
/// or a dominating `require` of a readable grant does (`rules::grant_dominated`).
// @ref LLP 3000.036#12 — a staff-only pass after `require exists staff[viewer]` reads every row it walks.
fn decided(schema: &Schema, program: &Program, scan: &Scan) -> bool {
    scan_visibility(schema, scan).uniform || crate::engine::rules::grant_dominated(schema, program, scan)
}

fn fanout(scan: Option<&Scan>, site: &str, reason: &str, rewrite: &str) -> Problem {
    let reason = reason.split_once("; ").map_or(reason, |(reason, _)| reason);
    let population = scan.map(|scan| format!("{} by {} (page bound {}): ", scan.table, scan.index, scan.take.maximum())).unwrap_or_default();
    Problem { code: "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT", site: site.into(), page_site: scan.map(|scan| scan.site.clone()), message: format!("{population}{reason}"), rewrite: format!("{rewrite}; for a single row use a point read by id (`table[id]`); for a global count/total read a maintained aggregate whose read rule explicitly admits the caller (public only when its totals may be public)") }
}

//! rule that is proven true by the scanned prefix (`decided_true`) costs no
//! probes; a rule whose deciding fields are pinned by the prefix (`uniform`) is
//! decided once for the whole range. Copied from Snapback 2's uniformity
//! analysis (LLP 2000.000 §5.1); the certificate that priced these is gone,
//! the analysis is not.

use crate::ir::{Bound, Expr, IndexKeyExpr, Input, Merge, Scan};
use crate::schema::{ColumnType, RuleExpr, RuleTerm, Schema, Table};
use crate::value::Value;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Visibility {
    /// One verdict serves every row of the scanned prefix.
    pub uniform: bool,
    /// That verdict is `true` before any row is read.
    pub decided_true: bool,
}

pub fn scan_visibility(schema: &Schema, scan: &Scan) -> Visibility {
    let Some(table) = schema.table(&scan.table) else { return Visibility::default() };
    let Some(index) = table.index(&scan.index) else { return Visibility::default() };
    let pinned = |name: &str| index.components.iter().zip(&scan.prefix).find_map(|(part, key)| (part.column().is_some_and(|column| column == name)).then(|| key.scalar()).flatten());
    visibility(&scan.table, table, &table.rules.read, &pinned)

}

// @ref LLP 3000.007#20.5 — a missing upsert may insert only when the complete held group and its key decide that no hidden target can exist.
pub fn upsert_absence(schema: &Schema, name: &str, index: &str, key: &[Expr]) -> Result<Visibility, &'static str> {
    let table = schema.table(name).ok_or("the target is online only")?;
    let sync = table.sync.as_ref().ok_or("the target is online only")?;
    if sync.horizon.is_some() { return Err("the target has a horizon"); }
    let rule = table.rules.read.device_audience_rule();
    // Public subset sync has no whole-table absence proof. Its group coverage
    // is a separate decision; do not infer it merely from the public read rule.
    if rule.is_uniformly_readable() && sync.audience != crate::schema::Audience::Public { return Err("the key's synced group is not established"); }
    let index = table.index(index).ok_or("the key does not pin readability")?;
    let pinned = crate::small_map::collect(index.components.iter().zip(key).filter_map(|(part, expression)| part.column().map(|column| (column, expression))));
    let visibility = prefix_visibility(name, table, &rule, &pinned);
    if !visibility.uniform { return Err("the key does not pin readability"); }
    Ok(visibility)
}

// @ref LLP 3000.007#18.1 — simplify self-witnesses, then pre-check only the leading conjuncts whose fields the scope pins, in evaluation order.
pub(super) fn prefix_decision(schema: &Schema, scan: &Scan) -> Option<RuleExpr> {
    let table = schema.table(&scan.table)?;
    let index = table.index(&scan.index)?;
    let pinned: BTreeMap<_,_> = crate::small_map::collect(index.components.iter().zip(&scan.prefix).filter_map(|(part, key)| part.column().zip(key.scalar())));
    if table.through.as_ref().is_some_and(|t| pinned.contains_key(&t.reference)) { return Some(table.rules.read.clone()); }
    let rule = simplify_prefix(&table.rules.read, &scan.table, table, &pinned);
    if matches!(rule, RuleExpr::Allow) { return None; }
    let mut terms = Vec::new();
    conjuncts(rule, &mut terms);
    let decided: Vec<_> = terms.into_iter().take_while(|term| {
        let mut fields = BTreeSet::new();
        term.fields(&mut fields);
        fields.iter().all(|field| pinned.contains_key(field))
    }).collect();
    (!decided.is_empty()).then_some(RuleExpr::And(decided))
}

// Flatten only conjunctions, preserving left-to-right short-circuit order.
fn conjuncts(rule: RuleExpr, out: &mut Vec<RuleExpr>) {
    match rule { RuleExpr::And(terms) => for term in terms { conjuncts(term, out); }, rule => out.push(rule) }
}

fn simplify_prefix(rule: &RuleExpr, name: &str, table: &Table, pinned: &BTreeMap<&String, &Expr>) -> RuleExpr {
    let pin = |name: &str| pinned.iter().find_map(|(key, value)| (key.as_str() == name).then_some(*value));
    if rule_known(rule, true, name, table, &pin) { return RuleExpr::Allow; }
    if rule_known(rule, false, name, table, &pin) { return RuleExpr::Deny; }
    match rule {
        RuleExpr::And(terms) => {
            let mut out = Vec::new();
            for term in terms { conjuncts(simplify_prefix(term, name, table, pinned), &mut out); }
            out.retain(|term| !matches!(term, RuleExpr::Allow));
            RuleExpr::And(out)
        },
        RuleExpr::Or(_) => {
            // Use the same self-witness absorption as uniformity, but remove
            // the absorbed field read from the expression we actually run.
            let terms = rule.disjuncts();
            let mut out: Vec<_> = terms.iter()
                .filter(|term| !terms.iter().any(|other| self_probe_absorbs(name, table, term, other)))
                .map(|term| simplify_prefix(term, name, table, pinned))
                .filter(|term| !matches!(term, RuleExpr::Deny))
                .collect();
            match out.len() {
                0 => RuleExpr::Deny,
                1 => out.pop().unwrap(),
                _ => RuleExpr::Or(out),
            }
        }
        RuleExpr::Not(inner) => {
            let inner = simplify_prefix(inner, name, table, pinned);
            negate_required_bool(&inner, table).unwrap_or_else(|| RuleExpr::Not(Box::new(inner)))
        }
        RuleExpr::Ne(left, right) => required_bool_equality(left, right, table, false).unwrap_or_else(|| rule.clone()),
        _ => rule.clone(),
    }
}

/// Required booleans have exactly two values, so their negated equality and
/// inequality forms can share one positive equality identity. Optional bools
/// retain their original expression because `null` is distinct from `false`.
// @ref LLP 3000.036.001#9 — prefix simplification and guard coverage use the same required-Boolean identity.
fn required_bool_equality(left: &RuleTerm, right: &RuleTerm, table: &Table, equal: bool) -> Option<RuleExpr> {
    [(left, right), (right, left)].into_iter().find_map(|(field, value)| {
        let (RuleTerm::Field(column), RuleTerm::Literal(Value::Bool(expected))) = (field, value) else { return None };
        matches!(table.columns.get(column), Some(ColumnType::Bool)).then(|| RuleExpr::Eq(
            RuleTerm::Field(column.clone()),
            RuleTerm::Literal(Value::Bool(if equal { *expected } else { !*expected })),
        ))
    })
}

fn negate_required_bool(rule: &RuleExpr, table: &Table) -> Option<RuleExpr> {
    match rule {
        RuleExpr::Allow => Some(RuleExpr::Deny),
        RuleExpr::Deny => Some(RuleExpr::Allow),
        RuleExpr::Eq(left, right) => required_bool_equality(left, right, table, false),
        RuleExpr::Ne(left, right) => required_bool_equality(left, right, table, true),
        _ => None,
    }
}
    }

            if text.is_empty() {

        }
        self.expr(expr, out)
    }

    pub(super) fn expr_as_reference(&mut self, expr: &A, out: &mut setup::Body, expected: &Ty) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
        let (value, ty) = self.expr_as_identity(expr, out, expected)?;
        Ok(self.row_identity(value, ty, expected))
    }

            }
        }
        (value, ty)
    }

//! A private population cannot answer a cross-row constraint for its writer.
// @ref LLP 3000.013#5.1 — aggregate consumers retain scan authorization and admission.
use super::*;
use snapback4_core::{engine::{admission, rules}, schema::{Constraint, RuleExpr, RuleTerm, Schema}};

impl BoundProgram {
    /// The shortest repair for a hidden-row population when one direct read
    /// disjunct exposes the viewer-owned slice.
    pub(crate) fn direct_viewer_repair(&self, schema: &Schema, problem: &admission::Problem) -> Option<String> {
        if problem.code != "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT" || self.program.kind != ir::ProgramKind::Mutation { return None; }
        let site = problem.page_site.as_ref()?;
        let scan = ir::scans(&self.program).into_iter().find(|scan| &scan.site == site)?;
        let table = schema.table(&scan.table)?;
        // Expiry can refuse an already-uniform scan for a different reason;
        // adding its existing viewer predicate would not repair that refusal.
        if rules::scan_visibility(schema, scan).uniform { return None; }
        let column = table.rules.read.disjuncts().iter().find_map(|rule| match rule {
            RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Field(column), RuleTerm::Viewer)
            | RuleExpr::Eq(RuleTerm::Viewer, RuleTerm::Field(column)) => Some(column.as_str()),
            _ => None,
        })?;
        Some(format!(
            "First add `.{column} = viewer` to this read's `where` predicate; that directly selects the read-rule audience and is the smallest qualifying repair. "
        ))
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.025#6-diagnostics-and-exact-documentation-changes — retain the admission repair before the qualified receipt-gap fallback.
    pub(crate) fn expiry_gap_diagnostic(&self, schema: &Schema, problem: &admission::Problem) -> Option<Diagnostic> {
        use snapback4_core::schema::ColumnType;
        if problem.code != "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT" || self.program.kind != ir::ProgramKind::Mutation { return None; }
        let site = problem.page_site.as_ref()?;
        let scan = ir::scans(&self.program).into_iter().find(|scan| &scan.site == site)?;
        let table = schema.table(&scan.table)?;
        if !table.is_expiring() || !rules::scan_visibility(schema, scan).uniform { return None; }
        let scan_index = table.index(&scan.index)?;
        let ordinal = scan_index.components.get(scan.prefix.len())?.column()?;
        if table.columns.get(ordinal) != Some(&ColumnType::Int) || !scan.orders_field(schema, ordinal) { return None; }
        let (parent, parent_table) = table.indexes.values().filter(|index| index.unique).find_map(|index| {
            if index.components.len() != 2 { return None; }
            let columns = [index.components[0].column()?, index.components[1].column()?];
            let parent = if columns[0] == ordinal { columns[1] } else if columns[1] == ordinal { columns[0] } else { return None; };
            let ColumnType::Ref { table: parent_table } = table.columns.get(parent)? else { return None; };
            // Consider every covering key, in either column order. An earlier
            // key on an unpinned parent cannot hide the applicable one.
            let scope = scan_index.components.iter().zip(&scan.prefix)
                .find_map(|(part, key)| (part.column() == Some(parent)).then(|| key.scalar()).flatten())?;
            rules::prefix_visibility(&scan.table, table, &table.rules.read, &[(parent, scope)].into()).uniform
                .then_some((parent, parent_table))
        })?;
        // A sender/ordinal equality may make the refused page uniform while
        // other positions in the parent group remain hidden. Never call those holes.
        // Uniformity proves one verdict for the scope, not that it is readable;
        // proving a dominating caller check needs control-flow/rule implication.
        let name = &scan.table;
        // Quarry comments keep the whole rewrite pasteable without hiding the
        // smaller repair that admits the author's original scan.
        let rewrite = format!("-- {}\n-- Fallback if the mutation must keep its prediction or effect ordering:\nfn skipExpired_{name}(scope: {parent_table}, initialPrefix: int, low: int):\n  prefix = initialPrefix\n  for i in range(0, 1024):\n    if prefix + 1 >= low:\n      break\n    if exists {name}[{parent} = scope, {ordinal} = prefix + 1]:\n      break\n    prefix = prefix + 1\n  return prefix", problem.rewrite);
        Some(Diagnostic::new(&self.sources.get(site)?.0, problem.code,
            format!("{}. For receipt gaps, try the admission repair below first. If the shape must stay refused, use bounded unique ordinal probes; a new schema can declare `{ordinal}: sequence by {parent}` with `unique {parent}, {ordinal}`. The helper's prefix justifies advancing a receipt only after the caller's own authority check (the membership check or the card's readable-message anchor). Call it inside the receipt merge, retain disjoint runs, and let an already-recorded run reach the helper again to resume after the 1,024-probe limit. For an unread badge use a row-keyed count; for general processing use a query or job (guide sequences)", problem.message),
            rewrite).guide("sequences"))
    }

    /// This is diagnostic selection only. The ordinary admission pass still
    /// owns the capped-scope case; neither path changes a rule or a scan.
    pub(crate) fn constraint_diagnostic(&self, schema: &Schema, problem: &admission::Problem) -> Option<Diagnostic> {
        if problem.code != "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT" || self.program.kind != ir::ProgramKind::Mutation { return None; }
        let site = problem.page_site.as_ref()?;
        if !self.constraint_domains.contains(site) { return None; }
        let scan = ir::scans(&self.program).into_iter().find(|scan| &scan.site == site)?;
        if rules::scan_visibility(schema, scan).uniform || capped_scope_decides(schema, scan) { return None; }
        let table = schema.table(&scan.table)?;
        let source = &self.sources.get(site)?.0;
        // @ref LLP 3000.036#11 — render the repairs against the author's own table and pins (app-farm patterns 6, 19).
        let pins: Vec<(String, String)> = table.index(&scan.index).map(|index| index.components.iter().zip(&scan.prefix)
            .filter_map(|(part, key)| {
                let column = part.column()?.clone();
                let value = match key.scalar()? { Expr::Variable(name) if !name.starts_with('$') => name.clone(), _ => column.clone() };
                Some((column, value))
            }).collect()).unwrap_or_default();
        let name = &scan.table;
        let group = pins.iter().map(|(column, _)| column.clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
        let key = pins.iter().map(|(_, value)| value.clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
        // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#9 — offer the direct viewer predicate before heavier structural repairs.
        let direct_audience = self.direct_viewer_repair(schema, problem).unwrap_or_default();
        let example = format!("declare one row per reserved unit with `unique resource, unit else TAKEN`, then insert those rows inside `{}`", self.program.name);
        // @ref LLP 3000.036#16.2 — wave 6 R2: `require not exists children…` before a delete is a zero count, not a capacity.
        let by = pins.iter().map(|(column, _)| format!(".{column}")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
        let absence = (!pins.is_empty()).then(|| absence_require(&self.program.body, site)).flatten().map(|code| format!(
            "an absence check over every {name} row, whoever may read it, is a zero count (it discloses only the count per {group}, never who): declare `view {name}Count: count {name} by {by}` with `read <- allow`, then in `{}` write `require {name}Count[{key}] = 0 else {code}` in place of the `not exists` (before a delete of the parent, this guard also silences N_DELETE_RESTRICTED; guide recipes, \"Booking\", `removeSlot`). Otherwise, ", self.program.name)).unwrap_or_default();
        Some(Diagnostic::new(source, "E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT",
            format!("`{}` can read only the {} its viewer may read (`{}`). A check over them would miss hidden {} rows, so it is refused. A point read of a full unique key (`exists {name}[…]`) is not refused, but it too sees only readable rows",
                self.program.name, scan.table, table.rules.read.quarry(), scan.table),
            format!("{direct_audience}{absence}for one known {name} row, use a point read by id (`{name}[id]`); for a global total, read a maintained aggregate whose explicit read rule admits this caller (public only if its totals may be public). use a constraint every write obeys, whoever wrote the clashing row: {example}; a clash rolls back the whole mutation. A hidden clash stays E_RULE; make the unit table public only if availability may be public, so a readable clash can return TAKEN. Or use a readable audience: check a public availability table if those rows may be public. {count}A `require` role guard does not make the population readable. See `snapback4 guide writes` for the per-night example", count = if pins.is_empty() || !absence.is_empty() { String::new() } else {
                // @ref LLP 3000.036#14.6 — wave 4 #15: the count view and the author's own capacity check, as code.
                let check = capacity_require(&self.program.body, site).map_or_else(|| format!("require {name}Count[{key}] < limit else FULL"),
                    |(op, bound, code)| format!("require {name}Count[{key}] {op} {bound} else {code}"));
                format!("For a count or capacity, keep a count whose read rule covers the writers (it discloses only the count per {group}, never who): `view {name}Count: count {name} by {by}` with `read <- allow`, then in `{}` `{check}` before the insert; the insert itself keeps the count current (guide indexes, \"Private lists\"). ", self.program.name)
            }))
            .guide("writes"))
    }
}

//! The binder's type model: what a Quarry expression is, statically, so a
//! program's arguments and result reach the client as TypeScript types by
//! inference (nothing is annotated, nothing is committed).

use crate::ast::{ScalarType, TypeKind};
use snapback4_core::ir::ArgType;
use snapback4_core::schema::{ColumnType, TextFormat};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Ty {
    Unknown,
    Null,
    Bool,
    Int,
    Time,
    Decimal(u8),
    Money(String, u8),
    Text(u32),
    Id,
    Principal,
    Ref(String),
    Bytes,
    Json,
    Image,
    Video,
    File,
    Enum(Vec<String>),
    Cursor,
    Optional(Box<Ty>),
    /// A bounded list of scalars; `max` bounds a loop over it.
    List(Box<Ty>, u32),
    /// One row of a table, present.
    Row(String),
    WriteRow(String),
    /// A bounded page of rows, in index order.
    Page(String, u32),
    /// A shaped page: at most `max` objects.
    Collection(Box<Ty>, u32),
    Object(BTreeMap<String, Ty>),
    /// A projection whose row base carries optional device metadata.
    RowShape(BTreeMap<String, Ty>),
    /// Object-spread fields with row metadata, but ordinary object wildcard order.
    RowObject(BTreeMap<String, Ty>),

}

impl Ty {
    /// A reassigned allocation is bounded by the heap meter, not its first literal's length.
    pub(crate) fn rebound(self) -> Ty {
        match self {
            Ty::Text(_) => Ty::Text(u32::MAX),
            // A known empty value stays empty, even at a loop header.
            Ty::List(_, 0) | Ty::Collection(_, 0) => self,
            Ty::List(item, _) => Ty::List(Box::new(item.rebound()), u32::MAX),
            Ty::Collection(item, _) => Ty::Collection(Box::new(item.rebound()), u32::MAX),
            Ty::Object(fields) => Ty::Object(fields.into_iter().map(|(name, ty)| (name, ty.rebound())).collect()),
            Ty::RowShape(fields) => Ty::RowShape(fields.into_iter().map(|(name, ty)| (name, ty.rebound())).collect()),
            Ty::RowObject(fields) => Ty::RowObject(fields.into_iter().map(|(name, ty)| (name, ty.rebound())).collect()),
            Ty::Optional(inner) => inner.rebound().optional(),
            other => other,
        }
    }

    pub fn optional(self) -> Ty {
        match self {
            Ty::Optional(_) | Ty::Null | Ty::Unknown => self,
            other => Ty::Optional(Box::new(other)),
        }
    }

    pub fn required(&self) -> Ty {
        match self {
            Ty::Optional(inner) => inner.as_ref().clone(),
            other => other.clone(),
        }
    }

    pub fn is_optional(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Ty::Optional(_) | Ty::Null)
    }

    pub fn is_bool(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Ty::Bool)
    }

    pub fn is_numeric(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Ty::Int | Ty::Time | Ty::Decimal(_) | Ty::Money(..))
    }

    pub fn is_identity(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Ty::Id | Ty::Principal | Ty::Ref(_))
    }

    pub fn from_scalar(scalar: &ScalarType) -> Ty {
        let base = match &scalar.kind {
            TypeKind::Cursor => Ty::Cursor,
            TypeKind::Text { max, .. } => Ty::Text(*max),
            TypeKind::Id => Ty::Id,
            TypeKind::Principal => Ty::Principal,
            TypeKind::Int | TypeKind::IntRange { .. } => Ty::Int,
            TypeKind::Decimal { scale } => Ty::Decimal(*scale),
            TypeKind::Money { currency, scale } => Ty::Money(currency.clone(), *scale),
            TypeKind::Time => Ty::Time,
            TypeKind::Bool => Ty::Bool,
            TypeKind::Json { .. } => Ty::Json,
            TypeKind::Bytes { .. } => Ty::Bytes,
            TypeKind::Image { .. } => Ty::Image,
            TypeKind::Video { .. } => Ty::Video,
            TypeKind::File { .. } => Ty::File,
            TypeKind::Enum { variants } => Ty::Enum(variants.clone()),
            TypeKind::Ref { table } => Ty::Ref(table.clone()),
            TypeKind::List { item, max, .. } => Ty::List(Box::new(Ty::from_scalar(item)), *max),
        };
        if scalar.optional { base.optional() } else { base }
    }

    pub fn from_column(kind: &ColumnType) -> Ty {
        match kind {
            ColumnType::Id => Ty::Id,
            ColumnType::Principal => Ty::Principal,
            ColumnType::Text { max } => Ty::Text(*max),
            ColumnType::Bytes { .. } => Ty::Bytes,
            ColumnType::Image { .. } => Ty::Image,
            ColumnType::Video { .. } => Ty::Video,
            ColumnType::File { .. } => Ty::File,
            ColumnType::Int | ColumnType::IntRange { .. } => Ty::Int,
            ColumnType::Enum { variants } => Ty::Enum(variants.clone()),
            ColumnType::Decimal { scale } => Ty::Decimal(*scale),
            ColumnType::Money { currency, scale } => Ty::Money(currency.clone(), *scale),
            ColumnType::Bool => Ty::Bool,
            ColumnType::Time => Ty::Time,
            ColumnType::Ref { table } => Ty::Ref(table.clone()),
            ColumnType::Json { .. } => Ty::Json,
            ColumnType::Optional(inner) => Ty::from_column(inner).optional(),
            ColumnType::List { of, max } | ColumnType::ListRange { of, max, .. } => Ty::List(Box::new(Ty::from_column(of)), *max),
        }
    }

    /// The name a diagnostic prints.
    pub fn name(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Ty::Unknown => "an unknown value".into(),
            Ty::Null => "null".into(),
            Ty::Bool => "bool".into(),
            Ty::Int => "int".into(),
            Ty::Time => "time".into(),
            Ty::Decimal(scale) => format!("decimal {scale}"),
            Ty::Money(currency, scale) => format!("money {currency} {scale}"),
            Ty::Text(max) => format!("text <={max}"),
            Ty::Id => "id".into(),
            Ty::Principal => "principal".into(),
            Ty::Ref(table) => format!("a {table} reference"),
            Ty::Bytes => "bytes".into(),
            Ty::Json => "json".into(),
            Ty::Image => "image".into(),
            Ty::Video => "video".into(),
            Ty::File => "file".into(),
            Ty::Enum(variants) => format!("enum({})", variants.iter().map(|v| format!("'{v}'")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")),
            Ty::Cursor => "cursor".into(),
            Ty::Optional(inner) => format!("{} ?", inner.name()),
            Ty::List(item, max) => format!("[{}] <={max}", item.name()),
            Ty::Row(table) => format!("a {table} row"),
            Ty::WriteRow(table) => format!("a {table} write result"),
            Ty::Page(table, max) => format!("a page of at most {max} {table} rows"),
            Ty::Collection(item, max) => format!("at most {max} of {}", item.name()),
            Ty::Object(fields) | Ty::RowShape(fields) | Ty::RowObject(fields) => format!("{{ {} }}", fields.keys().cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")),
        }
    }

    /// Whether a value of `self` may be stored where `expected` is declared.
    pub fn assignable_to(&self, expected: &Ty) -> bool {
        if self == expected {
            return true;
        }
        match (self, expected) {
            (Ty::Null, Ty::Optional(_)) => true,
            (Ty::Optional(inner), Ty::Optional(target)) => inner.assignable_to(target),
            (value, Ty::Optional(target)) => value.assignable_to(target),
            (Ty::Text(a), Ty::Text(b)) => a <= b,
            // @ref LLP 3000.007#20 — enum widening is static and total: every variant fits the text bound and character domain.
            (Ty::Enum(variants), Ty::Text(max)) => variants.iter().all(|v| v.chars().count() <= *max as usize && snapback4_core::engine::validate::disallowed_text_control(v).is_none()),
            // A text literal in an enum position is a variant; the binder
            // checks membership where it knows the literal.
            (Ty::Text(_), Ty::Enum(_)) => true,
            (Ty::Id, Ty::Ref(_)) | (Ty::Ref(_), Ty::Id) | (Ty::Id, Ty::Principal) | (Ty::Principal, Ty::Id) => true,
            (Ty::Ref(a), Ty::Ref(b)) => a == b,
            (Ty::Int, Ty::Time) | (Ty::Time, Ty::Int) => true,
            (Ty::Int, Ty::Decimal(_)) | (Ty::Int, Ty::Money(..)) => true,
            (a, b) if a.sequence().is_some() && b.sequence().is_some() => {
                let (a, am) = a.sequence().unwrap();
                let (b, bm) = b.sequence().unwrap();
                a.assignable_to(&b) && am <= bm
            },
            (Ty::Object(a) | Ty::RowShape(a) | Ty::RowObject(a), Ty::Object(b) | Ty::RowShape(b) | Ty::RowObject(b)) => a.len() == b.len() && a.iter().all(|(name, ty)| b.get(name).is_some_and(|target| ty.assignable_to(target))),
            (Ty::Enum(a), Ty::Enum(b)) => a.iter().all(|v| b.contains(v)),
            (Ty::Unknown, _) | (_, Ty::Unknown) | (_, Ty::Json) => true,
            _ => false,
        }
    }

    /// A heap-bound allocation can be written; the row validator checks its
    /// actual length. It cannot claim a smaller bound inside an inline helper.
    pub(crate) fn writable_to(&self, expected: &Ty) -> bool {
        match (self, expected) {
            (Ty::Optional(a), Ty::Optional(b)) => a.writable_to(b),
            (a, Ty::Optional(b)) => a.writable_to(b) || *a == Ty::Null,
            (Ty::Text(u32::MAX), Ty::Text(_)) => true,
            (Ty::List(a, am), Ty::List(b, bm)) => a.writable_to(b) && (*am == u32::MAX || am <= bm),
            _ => self.assignable_to(expected),
        }
    }

    /// Whether two values may meet in `=`, `!=` or a key position.
    pub fn comparable(&self, other: &Ty) -> bool {
        let a = self.required();
        let b = other.required();
        a == b || a.assignable_to(&b) || b.assignable_to(&a) || a == Ty::Null || b == Ty::Null
    }

    /// The type both branches can share. Row-kind conflicts are errors at
    /// their first join, including inside objects and collections.
    pub fn join(&self, other: &Ty) -> Result<Ty, JoinError> {
        self.join_inner(other, false)
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.1 — literals and concatenation share sound item joins.
    pub(crate) fn join_item(&self, other: &Ty) -> Result<Ty, JoinError> {

# LLP 3000.036.002: Intent-aware lints and production bootstrap

**Type:** RFC
**Status:** Implemented
**Systems:** Snapback 4 language diagnostics, CLI fixtures and production readiness, core audience-grant validation and development refusal traces
**Author:** Codex for Charlie Cheever (DIAG)
**Date:** 2026-10-13
**Revised:** 2026-10-14 (wave 12 declaration/diagnostic amendment §9; QDIAG amendments §§7–8; original implementation 2026-10-13)
**Related:** [LLP 3000.036](./3000.036-what-the-app-farm-asks-of-the-rule-language.rfc.md), [LLP 3000.036.000](./3000.036.000-sharing-shapes-at-sync-and-union-audiences.rfc.md), [LLP 3000.007](./3000.007-relaxed-quarry-and-explicit-residency.rfc.md) §20.6, [LLP 3000.011.003.000](./3000.011.003.000-offline-ready-application-starters.rfc.md) §8

## 1. Scope and motivation

Wave 10 fix-list #5, #7 and #15 expose disagreement between diagnostics and
execution: deliberate negative fixture tests look stale, one missing roster
produces many writer notes, and the recommended service-seat bootstrap fails
membership-grant validation. The coordinator authorizes this work and its
reviews. HS owns handshake/types, REL2 release lifecycle, DX2 starters/client
recipes, and PAGE2 general planner/rules expressiveness.

## 2. Service seats grant membership on the server

An entire positive branch `viewer = 'service:NAME'` with a nonempty name
satisfies the membership insert/update grant guard. The namespace is reserved:
accounts cannot mint it, and the operator mints a seat token against the
production store. This authority may enroll the first member or retarget a
mutable membership. An `and` branch containing that equality is likewise
restricted to the seat. An `or` requires every branch independently to prove
membership, a newly created group, or a seat. Negation, inequality, arbitrary
principal literals, and ordinary self-join remain insufficient.

Read-rule service grants already disappear before device audience inference
(LLP 3000.007 §20.6); this change adds no sync audience, capability or wire
format. Devices never hold service-seat partitions. Existing seat-session expiry and
revocation checks apply before a mutation is dispatched; no token lifecycle
changes are proposed. Only mintable service names (1–64 ASCII alphanumeric,
underscore or hyphen) qualify for production readiness; an impossible seat
keeps the root's N_NO_PRODUCTION_WRITER note rather than counting as a writer. Adding membership still
uses ordinary constraints, transactional logs and scope delivery/revocation.
An authenticated seat writes via an ordinary mutation, without system bypass.
The deploy card compiles a synced staff-roster example. The diagnostic's
inline recipe retains an already-online roster's residency and its entire
read predicate; references are resolved in the application's existing schema. Refused ordinary
self-join offers that trusted bootstrap beside the prior-member alternative,
without a redundant `(service and member) or member` rewrite. The offered
seat rule replaces the unsafe branch, never adds a seat to an otherwise
unprotected self-join.

## 3. Readiness notes identify blockers

Keep the positive-dependency least fixed point of LLP 3000.011.003.000 §8.
For blocked tables, dependencies are positive insert-rule probes/reference
terms and a read-through parent. Group mutually dependent tables; report one
note per root blocked component, listing the blocked descendants it governs.
Multiple roots can name a shared dependent. A table with no writer is a root
blocker even if its rule mentions another blocked table. Optional alternatives
remain conservative: this is advice, not a satisfiability/reachability theorem.
Native opaque jobs still prevent an absence claim. A persona-only schema
(with no production identity method) emits one production-identity note,
including the blocked tables when any exist, rather than one per table.

## 4. Fixture intent and guard visibility

`check` inspects shared cases only for operations declared by the checked
schema. Signature/decoding/validation failures whose runtime code is E_INPUT
are intentional when `expect` equals E_INPUT, so emit no argument-drift note.
Malformed JSON/case metadata remain authoring errors. Unknown operations
remain a hard error in `test`, including misspellings; read-only `check`
intentionally cannot distinguish shared newer operations from misspellings.
Expectations are the existing public refusal code, without a new phase field;
the runner prints the E_INPUT message/subcause on each passing negative case
so a negative assertion is reviewable without introducing another note. Saved runtime values
remain unknown. The fixture runner recognizes decoding/signature errors as
E_INPUT too; tests cannot claim success by skipping the case.

A program `exists` sees only caller-readable rows; a table-rule probe has
authority over all rows. Keep those semantics. Add N_UNREADABLE_PROBE on
negative requirements and conditional guards over private populations unless
the pins/preceding guards prove readability. Positive `require exists` is
itself an authorization check; retain its existing N_REQUIRE_HIDDEN analysis.
To cover values later used through aliases/returned helper booleans, inspect
point-existence observations when they happen, as well as mutation/job prefix
observations. Pure query prefix/search/seek values remain ordinary visible-hit
answers; trace guard-consumed bindings through aliases/objects/possible rebinding
and check those observations with their original authority. Inputs to a
guard-consuming helper/shape are conservatively tracked too (all inputs,
rather than an unsound partial parameter-use proof), including direct expression
inputs and guarded loop domains. Row-dependent candidate filters remain intentional
visible-hit query predicates (global gates lower to whole-page conditionals
and are checked); a computed boolean field passed to a guard is
still an observation. Snapshot markers exclude names in every actual argument,
so postorder substitution cannot match a fabricated name in another argument.
Helpers/shapes reached from a requirement inspect every direct input value,
including helpers that only invert it in their returned expression. A direct
positive `require exists` remains authorization. Traverse requirement
wrappers (members, objects, calls and nested conditionals), preserving direct
positive-existence authorization. Inline shape bases are inspected independently
of named-definition discovery. Expand object/write shorthand in analysis copies
before classifying global facts, discovering effects, checking shadowing, or
excluding/substituting/validating argument names; shorthand and explicit names
must have the same scope and proof behavior. Runtime expressions stay unchanged.
Name the target read
rule and explain that negative guards cannot enforce global absence. This is
advisory; an intentionally caller-visible guard can remain unchanged.

Follow reachable helpers, named shapes and spreads. Facts cross helper scopes
only through actual arguments or viewer/literals, with fresh intermediate names
to prevent caller/formal spelling collisions. A read-only helper can receive
snapshot evidence for an expression argument; a writing helper gets only scalar

# What Snapback 4 Does Not Do

Longer than the doing-list on purpose. Moving something off it means writing one
line naming what it unblocks and taking something off the doing-list in the same
change. Nothing comes off during slice one (LLP 3000 §3: the clock is four weeks).

## The bars

The bakeoff gates in [LLP 3000 §3](../llp/3000-snapback4.explainer.md) are the
bars: the loop bar, hub acquisition within 2× the measured floor, client bytes
under the competitor-anchored budgets, the six scenarios green in the simulator
on the hub fixture. Everything not required to pass them does not exist yet.

## Not building

- **A second authoring language.** Quarry, one spelling, copied from Snapback 2 (LLP 1004, LLP 1007 §4b). TypeScript is for seeds, journeys, effect bodies and the client.
- **Byte- and step-priced certification.** No closure, heap, output or step ceilings at `check`; the certificate certifies shape, uniformity, completeness class and prediction eligibility. Resources are metered at runtime (LLP 2000.000 §6).
- **A per-query result cache.** No range receipts, validators, halos, absence evidence, coverage spans, extent facts, held directories, fact integrity or swap journals. The client replicates declared partitions with one watermark each (LLP 2000.000 §7).
- **Engine-minted ids for client inserts, grants, ID slices.** Ids are client-minted, time-ordered, 128-bit; the engine mints for its own writes.
- **The `drain` protocol, follower-tab inbox rows, `defineItems`, `withHistory`, `mutationTarget`, `receipt.source`, `local.caughtUp`, `partial` reason codes.** The card (`packages/snapback4/src/contract.ts`) is the whole client vocabulary; `why` carries the rest.
- **`retain` as a receipt rule.** `until-revoked` and `delivered-history` survive as the client's leave policy on a scope tombstone.
- **JavaScript in the data plane.** Queries and mutations run in the Rust interpreter inside the SQLite transaction, and in the same interpreter on the client (host decided at week 3 by measurement, LLP 2000.000 §9). A *job* may be the app's own Rust, hosted as wasm through the interpreter's operations under the job's meter (LLP 3000.005, the Moves line below); a query or mutation may not.
- **An embedded JS engine for effects.** The data plane never calls out. `emit` writes the effect durably in the mutation's commit and an external worker holding a service token claims, performs and settles it over the wire (`snapback4/worker`); the four reference effects run on the builder's Node (LLP 2000.000 §10, decided 2026-09-13).
- **Committed generated code; an auth mode; a supervised bundler.** As Snapback 2 (`rules/NOT-DOING.md`): types by inference, personas not modes, `SNAPBACK_URL` is the client contract.
- **A TypeScript twin of the interpreter.** Retired by the author's ruling of 2026-09-13 (LLP 3000 §7): one implementation, in Rust, on every host — the core's SQLite under the native module, memory under wasm on the web with the host persisting each commit's changes. The web pays 312,924 B gzip before the diet where the twin's tier paid 16,842; the conformance obligation between two interpreters ends. Expo Go runs the online tier.
- **More than one hosted target, an admin console, media transcoding or thumbnails, push delivery itself (a worker's), cron syntax beyond `every N at HH:MM`, vector or relevance-ranked search (word-prefix search is in: `words(..)` and `matching`), federation, multi-region, device-to-device sync, at-rest encryption claims.** After the clock, on evidence.
- **General observability beyond `why`, `trace`, `logs`, `data`, `sql`, server operation latency, and bounded client subscription inspection.** The `sql` verb is read-only inspection of the developer's own store (LLP 3000.007 §8.8), never an application surface. Separately declared application SQL reads are admitted for increment D (LLP 3000.009 §6.2, §14.4; the 2026-09-16 Moves line below), not implemented by this inspection verb.
- **A guide corpus.** The compiler's facts, one language card and keyword cards, as Snapback 2; no freshness dates. Every card's Quarry is compiled by the suite and the language card is run, so a card cannot promise a form the parser refuses.

- **Partial union delivery, two group audiences, a public branch.** A union syncs principal-column branches and at most one group branch, each a whole disjunct of the read rule (LLP 3000.036.000.000); a branch with an extra condition, a second group or a `public` branch is refused with the rewrite, never partially delivered; service grants add no device audience (LLP 3000.007 §20.6). A union does not combine with delivered history, read-through children, synced or row-keyed views, owner keys, timelines, private field owners, acquisition windows or direct/inherited expiry on content or membership scopes.
- **Exact horizon maintenance.** The horizon bounds acquisition (a snapshot, a bootstrap); the log never evicts or back-fills to hold a device's group at exactly N rows. A local read past the acquired horizon by key says `complete: false`.

- **Clock expressions in rules.** A read rule compares with `=` and `!=` only; `.expiresAt > now` remains a mutation `require`. Stored lifetimes use `not before .col` for server-controlled opening and `expire at .col` for expiry. The engine publishes opening commits; devices receive no unopened payload. The supported compositions and explicit exclusions are in LLP 3000.036.003.
- **A jobs framework.** No priorities, worker pools or dead letters: one FIFO of runs, one chunk at a time, a refused chunk parked with its refusal. Actions, effects and scheduled actions carry per-operation retries, deadlines and cancellation, and a record per external step (LLP 3000.009 §5.2; the Moves line below). Missed period boundaries while a server is down fire once on return, not once per missed period.
- **Asset processing.** No transcoding, thumbnails, rungs or HEIC: the bytes are served as uploaded; JPEG, PNG, WebP and MP4 only; image dimensions and optional MP4 duration read from the header; MP4 dimensions are not extracted.
- **Search beyond word prefixes.** One tokenizer (NFC, lowercase, alphanumeric words), one index shape (`scope, words(cols), order.., id`), one read (`matching`): every term a prefix of some word, the first term's words merged as lanes, bounded by the meter in a uniform scope, at most 32 words in an admitted non-uniform scope. No stemming, no ranking by relevance, no phrase or mid-word matching, no per-language folding, no intersection index for the second term (it filters the page).
- **An identity provider.** Guests, password accounts, service seats, and sessions a service mints for accounts the application authenticated itself. No phone, OAuth, magic links or MFA in the engine: an application's worker verifies those and mints the session.
- **No multi-server presence, no presence history or last-seen storage, no broadcast event stream, no connection-bound rows.** `connected[p]` stays server-wide, counting held polls and their 35 s grace; a live query that may read it re-runs in the background about every 5 seconds to stay current (LLP 3000.018). Typing and viewing use short-lived, authorized ephemeral tables in one server process (LLP 3000.017); they never sync or decide durable invariants. A device does not know presence and says so.

## Process not doing

- **2026-09-28 — ordinary mixed search** (LLP 3000.028 §3.3, lane OS round 1).
  Admit the SDK's bounded merge of current server rows and certified Left images
  for the proved single time-ordered word page. This removes application-owned
  online/held selection for that shape. One server call per requested page;
  recomputation pays again from consumed positions. The coordinator shares the
  existing device read allowance. No durable search session, extra synced rows,
  new authority or additional allowance is admitted.

- **2026-09-28 — inferred current-scope word search** (LLP 3000.028 §3.3,
  lane OS). A single bare ordinary word page may derive the exact non-expiring
  membership audience for the existing compact server plan. This removes the
  requirement to repeat that audience predicate in this narrow server query.
  The compiler supplies a scoped words index when absent; it is an ordinary
  schema index, maintained on writes and on devices, with no extra synced rows
  or new authority. The device keeps its original bare scan. Round 0 left ordered composition
  and combined accounting outside its independent subset; round 1 above admits
  that bounded SDK composition. Durable search sessions remain excluded.
- **2026-10-12 — union sync audiences** (LLP 3000.036.000.000, workstream UNION, two blind review rounds). A table syncs to the union of principal-column audiences and one group audience; a device holds a row while any branch admits its viewer. What it unblocks: owner-or-team, buyer-or-seller and owner-or-staff tables offline for every reader, the shape three app farms asked for. Taken off: "one `sync` audience per table". Partial delivery, two groups and a public branch stay excluded (above).
- **2026-09-28 — explicit owner-key coverage** (LLP 3000.028 §3.4, Lane OK commission). A public window may opt into a compiler-owned, horizon-free principal key partition to answer ordinary own-key existence offline. Taken off: the exclusion of narrower platform key distribution beside one public window. General union audiences, full own-row replication and per-query absence caches remain excluded. The projection uses existing metered maintains, adoption and whole-partition publication; existing windows do not expand.
- **2026-09-26 — a live query keeps presence current** (LLP 3000.018). A 0.4.2 probe found an observed `connected[p]` reporting `fresh: true` while stale for over a minute, and a comparative builder polled around it. What it unblocks: online marks and presence-aware lists that stay current. Taken off: "a presence stream" as an exclusion for live queries; a presence API, last-seen storage and multi-server presence stay out. Under the author's standing authorization for reworks that make queries excellent (2026-09-25).

- **No drift registries, inventories, line-pinned diagnostics registries, claim digests or frozen-record gates.** Generated projections are built, not committed.
- **No gate bound to an exact commit; no push gated on a battery.** Five blocking checks in sixty seconds, run before push; everything slower on a schedule with bounded tickets.
- **No ceiling raised in slice one.** Budgets are anchored to a competitor's measured number and recorded once in the journal.
- **No standing panel** except the two blind reviews LLP 3000 decision 4 names (partition inversion; the meter's cut on non-uniform scans). The author explicitly commissioned the one-off LLP 3000.008 panel and disjoint Astra implementation lanes on 2026-09-14; its bounded disposition is recorded in that umbrella and LLP 3000 §7.
- **No new LLP number** without first extending LLP 3000 or LLP 2000.000; no spec without running code (`rules/RULES.md`: only implemented specs bind).
- **No second session on the core** during slice one; lanes take the periphery.
- **No test matrix as the primary harness.** The simulator is; real-browser and device witnesses cover only what it cannot reach.
- **No files over 1,500 lines**, including ones copied from Snapback 2. Split on
  the way in. The one exception is the package's published documents
  (`packages/snapback4/README.md` and its linked references): the rule exists to
  keep a *source* file reviewable, and the 0.2.25 calibration measured the cost of
  applying it to a document — splitting the README was that run's single largest
  scoring loss, because the builder then had four places to look instead of one
  (LLP 3000.007 §20.19). A published document is bounded by whether a builder can
  find one way in, not by a line count; the census that enforces this rule covers
  source, and says so.

## Deliberately worse

- No compatibility with Snapback 1 or Snapback 2 apps, packages or on-disk formats.
- No API stability before the clock; every publish is `0.0.x`.
- Sparse prose documentation; the diagnostics and the recipes carry the load.
- One hosted target, SQLite in the production CLI, one platform binary at a time. A separately enabled Postgres evaluation adapter is not a hosted/deployable target (Moves below).

## Moves

- **2026-10-13 — stored lower lifetimes (`not before`) are commissioned by PAGE2** (LLP 3000.036.003). This unblocks timed disclosure without an application publication job. Per-application jobs that flip a publication flag leave this admitted path; clock expressions in rules, captured lower lifetimes for read-through children, and boundary recounts for maintained data remain excluded. HS owns handshake transport; PAGE2 declares the new semantic capability.

- **2026-10-06 — exact Following history (FH delegated round-1 ruling).**
  Admit a Following-specific server traversal and bounded volatile frontier/replay
  state under LLP 3000.026 §9. The approved design reads exact history online
  from the first page; the SDK will own continuation. The first milestone is internal event metadata
  and the oracle, with no public completeness claim. Taken off: a blanket ban on
  state for this one expiring read. General result caches, resumable queries,
  device traversal, inbox coverage certificates and history-only blocks remain

# Rules

**Snapback 2 optimizes the edit-to-verified loop — the agent's building an app on it, and ours building it.**

Speed is the constraint. Everything below exists to keep the edit-to-verified loop short
and to stop this repository accreting apparatus faster than anyone can remove it. These
rules bind `snapback2/` and the LLPs numbered 1000 and up; Snapback 1 is baselined, not
exempt, and its numbers may only fall.

Each rule is **[check]** (enforced by `caps`) or **[review]** (enforced by a human).

## Budgets — every budget is a trade, not a limit

- **5 blocking checks, 60s total.** A sixth requires deleting one, in the same PR. **[check]**
- **59 documents in the working set** (`llp/current/`). Today's count. A 60th requires
  archiving one — which is just removing the link. Snapback 2 aims to leave this at 15;
  Snapback 1's links are archived at promotion. **[check]**
- **12 documents in the foundation** (`llp/foundation/`). **[check]**
- **This file: 700 words.** If it grows, something becomes a check or stops being a rule. **[check]**
- **1,500 lines per source file, baseline 204.** Generated files exempt — and generated
  files are built, not committed; so are benchmark run records under `benchmarks/runs/`,
  which are evidence, not source. The baseline is Snapback 1's oversize count on the day
  the rule landed; it may not grow, and `snapback2/` contributes zero to it. **[check]**

## Blocking checks

`caps` · `ref-check` · `snapback2/scripts/test.sh` · `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs --check` · `check-inventories`

## Loop shape

- **Every check reports all failures in one run.** Fail-fast is banned. **[check]**
- **Nothing blocks on anything slower than 60 seconds.** Slow verification runs on a
  schedule, attributed to the breaking commit, and files a bounded set of issues. **[review]**
- **Fix loops get 3 rounds.** Then stop: escalate to a human or descope. **[review]**

## Time budgets

Tracked every run of `snapback2/scripts/measure.mjs` (appends `snapback2/metrics/loop.jsonl`).
A regression is a P0 with a name on it.

| | budget |
|---|---|
| Incremental rebuild after a one-line edit | 15s |
| Test what you just changed | 30s |
| Blocking gate suite | 60s |
| Full build, warm cache | 5 min |
| **`snapback2 check` on a program (the agent's product latency)** | **1s** |
| **`snapback2 doctor` boot-to-ready** | **0.5s** |

## Scope

- **`NOT-DOING.md` is binding.** Moving something onto the doing-list means writing why
  and taking something off. **[review]**
- **Delete; don't deprecate.** No compat shims or migration paths before promotion. **[review]**
- **Nothing is compiled, transpiled, or generated at runtime that could be built ahead of
  time.** **[review]**
- **A spec needs an implementer and a date, or it isn't written.** **[review]**
- **Only implemented specs bind.** A document with no running code behind it is a
  proposal, and a proposal cannot block a PR or justify a check. **[review]**

## Agents

- **Agents remove apparatus freely and add none.** An agent PR that adds a check, script,
  registry, config file, or design doc needs explicit human approval saying so. **[review]**
- **2026-09-06 session exception:** the user delegated the search implementation
  decisions; one `snapback2-core/build.rs` may generate pinned Unicode tables at
  build time, alongside the existing package build. No new gate, registry,
  runtime generator, or Unicode dependency is authorized by this exception. **[review]**
- **Snapback 2 LLPs are numbered 1000 and up**; `llp-create` must be told. **[review]**
- **Snapback 4 LLPs are numbered 3000 and up** (`snapback4/`, LLP 3000); it adopts these budgets
  and loop shape as its own and keeps its scope in `snapback4/NOT-DOING.md`. **[review]**

## Shared machines

- Warm, named lanes, one per stream of work. Never clone fresh; reuse the worktree.
- **Never `git stash`.** Use a temporary commit.
- Kill only PIDs you recorded at launch. Never by name or pattern.

//! Column and parameter types, including precise unsupported-default repairs.
use super::Parser;
use crate::{ast::*, diag::{Fallible, Site, syntax, syntax_with}, lexer::Kind, print};
impl Parser {
    pub(super) fn parse_args(&mut self) -> Fallible<Vec<ArgDecl>> {
        self.take("(")?;
        let mut args = Vec::new();
        while !self.at(")") {
            let name = self.peek().clone();
            let binding = self.local_name()?;
            self.take(":")?;
            let type_site = self.peek().site.clone();
            let type_ = self.parse_type(false).map_err(|mut d| {
                if d.mechanical && d.message.starts_with("once is a column modifier") {
                    // Nested element types need a whole-list rewrite, not an argument fragment.
                    if d.site == type_site { d.site = name.site.clone(); d.rewrite = format!("{binding}: {}", d.rewrite); }
                    else { d.mechanical = false; }
                }
                d
            })?;
            if self.at("=") || self.at("default") {
                let at = self.peek().site.clone();
                self.position += 1;
                let fallback = self.expression(0, &[",", ")"])?;
                let mut optional = type_.clone(); optional.optional = true;
                return Err(syntax_with(&at, "operation parameters have no literal defaults; omission is null for an optional parameter",
                    format!("declare `{binding}: {}` and bind `{binding}Value = {binding} ?? {}` at the start of the body", print::scalar_type(&optional), print::expression(&fallback))).guide("types"));
            }
            args.push(ArgDecl { name: binding, type_, site: name.site });
            if !self.maybe(",") {
                break;
            }
        }
        self.take(")")?;
        Ok(args)
    }

    pub(super) fn parse_type(&mut self, column: bool) -> Fallible<ScalarType> {
        let site = self.peek().site.clone();
        let mut kind;
        if self.maybe("[") {
            let item = self.parse_type(column)?;
            self.take("]")?;
            // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.4 — list ranges share text's inclusive spelling.
            let bounds_error = |site: &Site| syntax_with(site, "list bounds require <=N or an inclusive a..b range", "write [T] <=N or [T] a..b, for example [int] 1..8").guide("types");
            let number = |parser: &mut Self| -> Fallible<u32> {
                if parser.at("-") {
                    return Err(syntax(&parser.peek().site, "list bounds must be nonnegative integers"));
            inserts.push(format!("{name} ({})", site.reason));
        }
        let reads = horizons::reads(fact);
        if fact.predicts.as_deref() == Some("eligible") && !reads.is_empty() {
            horizons.push(format!("{name} ({})", reads.join(", ")));
        }
    }
    let mut parts = Vec::new();
    // @ref LLP 3000.036#12 — wave 2 (075): the summary is information, not a warning.
    if !never.is_empty() { parts.push(format!("{} {} server-run (online app: no action): {}", if never.len() == 1 { "1 mutation".to_owned() } else { format!("{} mutations", never.len()) }, if never.len() == 1 { "is" } else { "are" }, never.join(", "))); }
    if !inserts.is_empty() { parts.push(if detailed { format!("{} {} insert arms that never predict: {}", inserts.len(), if inserts.len() == 1 { "mutation has" } else { "mutations have" }, inserts.join(", ")) } else { format!("{} mutations have insert arms that may queue", inserts.len()) }); }
    if !horizons.is_empty() { parts.push(if detailed { format!("{} {} eligible, but these reads queue without a row past a horizon: {}", horizons.len(), if horizons.len() == 1 { "mutation" } else { "mutations" }, horizons.join(", ")) } else { format!("{} eligible mutations may queue past a horizon", horizons.len()) }); }
    (!parts.is_empty()).then(|| format!("{}{} — snapback4 why <op>", if bound.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_SYNC") { "provisional while E_SYNC is unresolved: " } else { "" }, parts.join("; ")))
}

pub(super) fn maintain_notes(catalog: &Catalog, schema: &Schema) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#6.8 — check states inheritance; test --residency measures the adopted fixture's cold rows.
    let mut notes: Vec<_> = schema.synced().filter_map(|(name, table, sync)| {
        let source = table.residency.inherited_from.as_ref()?;
        match &sync.audience {
            Audience::Column(_) => return None,
            Audience::Target { table: target, .. } => {
                if let Ok(binding) = snapback4_core::schema::audience_binding(schema, name, table, sync)
                    && schema.tables[target].cap(&binding.columns).is_some() && schema.maintain_for(name)?.by.len() == binding.columns.len() { return None; }
            }
            Audience::Public => {}
        }
        let readers: Vec<_> = schema.operations.iter().filter(|(_, fact)| fact.predicts.as_deref() == Some("eligible") && fact.sites.iter().any(|site| site.table == name)).map(|(name, _)| name.as_str()).collect();
        let consequence = if readers.is_empty() { "no currently eligible mutation reads it".into() } else { format!("{} would stop predicting if {name} goes `online only`", readers.join(", ")) };
        Some(Diagnostic::new(&catalog.site_for(&format!("tables.{name}")), "N_MAINTAIN_SYNCED", format!("maintain {name}: {} inherited from {source}, no horizon; one value row per {} reaches {}; {consequence}", sync.line(), schema.maintain_for(name)?.by.join(", "), if sync.audience == Audience::Public { "every device" } else { "every member of the group" }), "keep inherited sync for local readers and offline absence coverage, or add `online only` and lose that offline coverage; measure cold rows with `snapback4 test --residency`; guide maintains; guide offline-interactions").guide("residency"))
    }).collect();
    if notes.len() > 1 {
        let message = format!("{} synced maintains:\n{}", notes.len(), notes.iter().map(|note| format!("  {} (site {})", note.message, note.site)).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\n"));
        notes[0].message = message;
        notes.truncate(1);
    }
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#8 — item 7: a readable maintain can disclose a hidden source's write delta.
    for maintain in &schema.maintains {
        // @ref LLP 3000.036.002#9 — only an explicit reviewed-disclosure annotation suppresses this audit note.
        if catalog.maintains.get(&maintain.target).is_some_and(|decl| decl.reviewed_disclosure.is_some()) {
            continue;
        }
        let (Some(source), Some(target)) = (schema.table(&maintain.source), schema.table(&maintain.target)) else { continue };
        if source.rules.read.is_uniformly_readable() || target.rules.read == RuleExpr::Deny { continue; }
        // Same read predicate over the grouped fields cannot give a hidden writer this aggregate.
        let mut fields = BTreeSet::new();
        source.rules.read.fields(&mut fields);
        if source.through.is_some() && fields.iter().all(|field| maintain.bare_key(field) || maintain.aliases.values().any(|c| c == field)) {
            let derived = source.rules.read.map_fields(&|field| maintain.aliases.iter().find(|(_,capture)| capture.as_str() == field).map_or_else(|| field.into(),|(output,_)| output.clone()));
            if derived == target.rules.read { continue; }
        }
        if target.rules.read == source.rules.read && !fields.contains("id") && fields.iter().all(|field| maintain.bare_key(field)) { continue; }
        // An old-image guard that entails the source read rule does not widen write authority.
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#8 — item 7(a): an unnamed update rule judges the old image too.
        let update = if source.update_transition { source.rules.update.clone() } else { source.rules.update.old_and_next() };
        if implies(&source.rules.insert, &source.rules.read) && implies(&source.rules.delete, &source.rules.read) && implies(&update, &old_read(&source.rules.read)) { continue; }
        notes.push(Diagnostic::new(&catalog.site_for(&format!("tables.{}", maintain.target)), "N_MAINTAIN_DELTA", format!("maintain {} may disclose the delta of a hidden {} row: insert/delete and a potentially wider update rule affect this readable target; filter/key/value dependencies: {}", maintain.target, maintain.source, maintain.dependencies().into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")), "treat the view as a declared read channel; restrict its read rule or the source update rule if the delta is private; after reviewing an intentional disclosure, add `disclosure reviewed 'rationale'` to the maintain").guide("rules"));
    }
    notes
}

/// The cold-snapshot report identifies which maintains the grouped fact names.
pub fn maintain_note_names(note: &Diagnostic, name: &str) -> bool {
    note.code == "N_MAINTAIN_SYNCED" && note.message.lines().any(|line| line.trim_start().starts_with(&format!("maintain {name}:")))
}
